translations.text: The words of Jeremiah son of Hilkiah, one of the priests in Anathoth in the land of Benjamin.
To whom the word of the Lord came in the days of Josiah son of Amon, king of Judah, in the thirteenth year of his reign.

It also came in the days of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, until the completion of the eleventh year of Zedekiah son of Josiah, king of Judah, until Jerusalem was taken captive in the fifth month.
The word of the Lord came to me, saying:
Before I formed you in the womb, I knew you; before you came out of the womb, I consecrated you and appointed you a prophet to the nations.
I said, “Please, Lord God! Look, I do not know how to speak, because I am a child.”
The Lord said to me, “Do not say, ‘I am a child,’ because you will go to everyone to whom I send you, and you will speak everything I command you.
Do not be afraid of them, because I am with you to rescue you, declares the Lord.”
The Lord stretched out his hand and touched my mouth. The Lord said to me, “Look, I have put my words in your mouth.
See, today I have given you authority over nations and kingdoms, to uproot and tear down, to overthrow and destroy, to build and plant.
The word of the Lord came to me, saying, “What do you see, Jeremiah?” I said, “I see an almond branch.”
The Lord said to me, “You have seen correctly, because I am hastening to carry out my word.”
The word of the Lord came to me a second time, saying, “What do you see?” I said, “I see a boiling pot, with its face turned away from the north.”
The Lord said to me, “From the north disaster will be unleashed upon all the inhabitants of the land.

“For look, I am sending and summoning all the families of the kingdoms of the north,” says the Lord. “They will come, and each will set his throne at the entrance to Jerusalem’s gates, against all its surrounding walls and against all the towns of Judah.
I will pronounce my judgments against them for all their wickedness, because they have abandoned me, burned incense to other gods, and worshiped the work of their own hands.
But you, fasten your belt, stand up, and tell them everything I command you. Do not be afraid of them, or I will shatter you before them.

Look, today I have made you like a fortified city, an iron pillar, and a bronze wall against the whole land: against the kings of Judah, their officials, their priests, their prophets, and all the people of the land.
They will fight against you, but they will not overcome you, because I am with you to rescue you, declares the Lord.”
The word of the Lord came to me, saying:

Go and proclaim in Jerusalem’s hearing: “This is what the Lord says: I remember the devotion of your youth, the love of your endurance, when you followed me in the wilderness, in a land that was not sown.
Israel was holy to the Lord, the firstfruits of his harvest. All who devour them will be held guilty; disaster will come upon them,” says the Lord.
Hear the word of the Lord, house of Jacob and all the families of the house of Israel.
This is what the Lord says: “What injustice did your ancestors find in me, that they went far from me, followed what was nothing, and gained nothing?

They did not say, ‘Where is the Lord, who brought us up from the land of Egypt, who led us through the wilderness, through a ruined and desolate land, through a barren land of death’s shadows, through a land that no one crossed and where no human being lived?’
I brought you into a fertile land to eat its fruit and its good things. But you came and defiled my land and made my inheritance unclean.

The priests did not say, ‘Where is the Lord?’ Those who handled the law did not know me. The shepherds dealt falsely with me, the prophets prophesied by Baal, and they followed what could bring no benefit.
Therefore I will bring a case against you, declares the Lord, and I will bring a case against your children’s children.
Cross over to the islands of Kittim and see; send to Kedar and examine carefully. See whether anything like this has happened.
Do nations exchange their gods, though they are not gods? Yet my people have exchanged their glory for what brings no benefit.
Be astonished at this, heavens! Tremble and be very afraid, says the Lord.
For my people have committed two evils: they have abandoned me, the spring of living water, and gone and dug cisterns for themselves—cracked cisterns that cannot hold water.
Is Israel a slave, or was he born into slavery in the household? Why has he become plunder?
Lions will roar over him and raise their voices. They will make his land a ruin, and his towns will lie desolate, without inhabitants.
The people of Memphis and Tahpanhes will also feed on you, head by head.
Look, this will happen to you because you abandoned the Lord your God while he was leading you along the way.
And now, why are you taking the road to Egypt to drink the waters of Shihor? And why are you taking the road to Assyria to drink the waters of the River?

Your wickedness will discipline you, and your turning away will rebuke you. Know and see how evil and bitter it is that you have abandoned the Lord your God and have not feared me,” says the Lord, the mighty God.
“For long ago I broke your yoke and snapped your bonds, and you said, ‘I will no longer serve another god.’ Yet on every high hill and beneath every leafy tree you wander and act as a prostitute.
I planted you as a choice vine, entirely from genuine seed. How then have you turned against me and rebelled like a foreign vine?
Even if you wash yourself with soda and use much sulfur, your sins remain stained upon you before me,” says the Lord God.
“How can you say, ‘I have not defiled myself, and I have not followed Baal’? Look at your ways in the valleys, and recognize what you have done. You have raised your voice, you who twist your paths.

Like a wild donkey accustomed to the wilderness, in its own desire, you have sniffed the wind. Like a jackal, who can turn her back? Whoever seeks her need not wear himself out; he will find her on her paths.
Keep your feet from going barefoot and your throat from thirst. But you said, ‘I have taken courage; I am unwilling, for I love strangers, and I will follow them.’
As a thief is ashamed when he is caught, so the people of Israel have been ashamed—they, their kings, their officials, their priests, and their prophets.

They say to wood, “You are our father,” and to stone, “You gave birth to us.” For they have turned their backs to me, not their faces. Yet in the time of their trouble they say, “Rise up, help me, and save me!”
Where are your gods that you made for yourself? Let them rise up and save you in the time of your trouble! For your gods have become as numerous as your towns, Judah.
Why do you bring a case against me? You have all dealt falsely with me, says the Lord.
In vain I struck your children; they did not accept correction. The sword devoured your prophets like a destroying lion.
You people of this generation, hear the word of the Lord! Have I been a wilderness to Israel, or like a devastated land? Why have my people said, “We have gone down; we will no longer come to you”?
Does a young woman forget her ornaments, or a bride her finery? Yet my people have forgotten me for more days than can be counted.
Why do you keep arranging your paths to seek love? Look, you have even learned evil in your ways.
Also on your hands was found the blood of innocent poor people. You did not find them breaking in, but beneath every tree.
Yet you said, “I am innocent; therefore he has turned his anger away from me.” Look, I am bringing you to judgment because you said, “I have not sinned.”
Why do you demean yourself so much by changing your ways? You will be put to shame by Egypt too, just as you were put to shame by Assyria.
You will also leave this place with your hands on your head, because the Lord is angry with those you trust, and you will not prosper through them.

If a man divorces his wife, and she leaves him and becomes another man's wife, will he return to her again? Surely that land would be thoroughly defiled. Yet you have prostituted yourself with many lovers. Return to me, says the Lord.

Lift your eyes to the paths and look: where have you not been defiled? You sat along the roads waiting for them, like a raven in the wilderness. You defiled the land with your prostitution and your wickedness.
The showers were withheld, and there was no spring rain. Yet you had the forehead of a prostitute and refused to accept correction.
Look, now you call to me, ‘My Father, you have been my guardian since my youth.’
‘Will he hold on to his anger forever? Will he keep it for all eternity?’ Look, you have spoken, but you have done evil and persisted in it.
The Lord said to me in the days of King Josiah, “Have you seen what the community of Israel has done? She went up every high mountain and beneath every leafy tree and prostituted herself there.”
I said that after she had done all these things she would return to me, but she did not return. Her sister Judah saw her deceit.

She saw everything she had done. Because the community of Israel committed adultery, I divorced her and gave her a certificate of divorce. Yet her deceitful sister Judah was not afraid; she too went and prostituted herself.
Because she treated her prostitution lightly, she defiled the land and committed adultery with stones and wood.
Even after all this, her deceitful sister Judah did not return to me with her whole heart, but only in pretense, says the Lord.
The Lord said to me, ‘The people of Israel have shown themselves more righteous than their deceitful sister Judah.’

Go and proclaim these words in the north, and say: “Return, community of Israel, says the Lord. I will not set my face harshly against you, for I am good, says the Lord, and I will not remain angry forever.”
Only acknowledge your sins: you have sinned against the Lord your God and scattered your paths among strangers beneath every leafy tree. You have not listened to my voice, says the Lord.
Return, repentant children, says the Lord, for I have desired you. I will take you, one from a town and two from a clan, and bring you to Zion.
I will give you shepherds after my own heart, and they will shepherd you with knowledge and understanding.

When you become fruitful and multiply in the land in those days, says the Lord, they will no longer say, “The ark of the covenant of the Lord.” It will not come to mind; they will not remember it or seek it out, nor will it be made again.
At that time they will call Jerusalem the throne of the Lord, and all the nations will place their hope in the name of the Lord. They will no longer follow the desires of their evil hearts.
In those days the house of Judah will go with the house of Israel, and together they will come from the northern land to the land that I gave their ancestors as an inheritance.

I said, “I will count you among my children and give you a choice land, an inheritance of the forces of the nations’ armies.” And I said, “You will call me ‘My Father,’ and you will not turn away from following me.”
Yet just as a woman is unfaithful to her husband, so the children of Israel have been unfaithful to me, says the Lord.
A sound was heard on the paths: the weeping and pleading of the house of Israel, because they had made their ways crooked and forgotten the Lord their God.
Return, you children who have turned away, and I will heal your waywardness. And they said, “Here we are, yours, because you are the Lord our God.”
Truly, the heights and the strength of the mountains are a deception. Truly, the salvation of Israel is in the Lord our God.
Shame has consumed the labor of our fathers from their youth—their sheep, their cattle, their sons, and their daughters.

Let us lie down in our shame, and let our disgrace cover us, because we and our fathers have sinned against the Lord our God, from our youth until today, and we have not obeyed the voice of the Lord our God.
If you return, Israel, says the Lord, return to me. If you remove your uncleanness from before me, you will not be shaken.
And you shall swear, “As the Lord lives,” in truth, justice, and righteousness. The nations will be blessed through him, and in him they will boast.
For this is what the Lord says to the men of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem: “Light a lamp for yourselves, and do not sow among thorns.”

Circumcise yourselves for the Lord, and remove the foreskin of your hearts, men of Judah and inhabitants of Jerusalem, lest my wrath break out like fire and burn with no one to extinguish it, because of your evil deeds.
Declare it in Judah and proclaim it in Jerusalem. Say, “Blow the trumpet in the land!” Cry aloud and say, “Gather together, and let us enter the fortified towns!”
Raise a banner toward Zion. Make yourselves strong, and do not stand still, for I am bringing disaster from the north, and great destruction.
A mighty king comes up like a lion from its thicket. A destroyer of nations has set out and left his place to turn your land into a ruin. Your towns will be desolate, with no one living in them.
Because of this, put on sackcloth, leap about, and wail, for the Lord’s fierce anger has not turned away from you.
“On that day,” says the Lord, “the kings and rulers will lose heart. The priests will be appalled, and the prophets will be astonished.”
Then I said, “Please, Lord God! You have truly deceived this people and Jerusalem by saying, ‘You will have peace,’ while the sword has reached our very lives.”
At that time it will be said to this people and to Jerusalem: “Like a wandering wind on the paths of the wilderness is the way of the daughter of my people—not for winnowing or gathering.”
A wind stronger than these will come to me. Now I too will pronounce my judgments against them.”
Look! He will rise like a cloud, and his chariot is like a whirlwind. His horses are swifter than eagles. Woe to us, for we have been plundered!
Wash the evil from your heart, Jerusalem, so that you may be saved. How long will your evil thoughts lodge within you?
For a voice announces news from Dan and proclaims distress from the mountain of Ephraim.
Make it known to the nations and proclaim it to Jerusalem: “Look, multitudes are coming from a distant land, and they will raise their voices against the towns of Judah.”
Like guards of fields, they surround her on every side, because she has rebelled against me, says the Lord.
Your ways and your deeds have brought these things upon you. This is your evil: it is bitter and has reached your very heart.
My insides, my insides are in pain, and so are the walls of my heart! My heart pounds within me and will not be still, for my soul has heard the sound of the trumpet and the battle cry.
Destruction upon destruction will come, for the whole land has been plundered. Suddenly my tent was plundered, and my tent curtains fell.
How long must I see people fleeing and hear the sound of the trumpet?
For my people have become foolish and do not know me. They are senseless children and have no wisdom. They are skilled at evil, but they do not know how to do good.
I looked at the earth, and there it was, waste and empty; I looked at the heavens, and their light was gone.
I saw the mountains, and they were shaking, and all the hills were torn apart.
I looked, and there was no human being, and all the birds of the sky had fled.
I looked, and there was Carmel, laid waste like a wilderness, and all its towns were uprooted before the Lord and before his fierce anger.
For this is what the Lord says: “The whole land will be devastated, but I will not make a complete end of it.
Because of these things the earth will mourn, and the heavens above will grow dark. As for all that I have spoken and planned, I will not regret it or turn back from it.
At the sound of the horsemen and archers, the whole town fled. They entered the thickets and climbed the cliffs. All the towns were abandoned, and no one lives in them.

And you, plundered one, what will you do? Though you dress in scarlet, adorn yourself with gold ornaments, and paint your eyes with eye paint, you beautify yourself in vain. Your companions have abandoned you, and they seek your life.

For I heard a cry like that of a sick woman, and anguish like that of a woman in labor about to give birth—the voice of the daughter of Zion, distraught and spreading out her hands, saying, “Woe to me! My soul is distraught over my slain!”
Go around the streets of Jerusalem. Look and find out; search her public squares. If you can find a man, if there is anyone who acts justly and seeks faithfulness, I will forgive her.
Even if they say, “As the Lord lives,” they are certainly swearing falsely.
Lord, your eyes look for faithfulness. You struck them, but they felt no pain. You consumed them, but they refused to accept correction. They made their faces harder than stone and refused to return.
And I said, “Because they are poor, they have gone astray, for they do not know the way of the Lord or the judgment of their God.”
“I will go to the leaders and speak with them, for they know the way of the Lord and the judgment of their God.” But surely all of them together have broken the yoke and snapped the bonds.

Therefore a lion from the forest will crush them, and evening wolves will tear them apart. A leopard will lie in wait around their towns; everyone who comes out of them will be torn apart, because their sins have multiplied and they have stubbornly refused to turn back.

How can I forgive you? Your children have abandoned me and sworn by those who are not gods. I fed them until they were full, but they committed adultery and jostled one another in the prostitutes’ house.
They were like strong, adulterous stallions, each neighing after his neighbor’s wife.
“Shall I not punish them for these things?” says the Lord. “Shall I not take vengeance on a nation like this?”
Climb her walls and tear them down, but do not destroy her completely. Leave her foundations, because they belong to the Lord.
“For the people of Israel and the people of Judah have dealt utterly falsely with me,” says the Lord.
They have been false to the Lord and say, “It is not he. No disaster will come upon us, and we will see neither sword nor famine.
The prophets will become a whirlwind, and those who have no word—so it will be done to them.”
Therefore this is what the Lord, the mighty God, says: “Because you have spoken these words, look, I am making my words in your mouth a fire, and this people wood, and it will consume them.”

“Look, I am bringing a nation from far away against you, house of Israel,” says the Lord. “It is a mighty nation, an ancient nation, a nation whose language you do not know and whose speech you cannot understand.”
Their throats are like open graves, and all of them are mighty warriors.

It will devour your harvest and your bread; it will devour your sons and daughters; it will devour your sheep and cattle; it will devour your vines and fig trees. With the sword it will impoverish the fortified towns in which you trust.
“Yet even in those days,” says the Lord, “I will not wipe you out.

And when you say, “Why has the Lord our God done all these things to us?” you are to tell them, “This is what the Lord says: Because you abandoned me and served foreign gods in your own land, so you will serve foreigners in a land that is not yours.”
Declare this in the house of Jacob and proclaim it in Judah, saying:
Hear this, foolish people without understanding, who have eyes but do not see, who have ears but do not hear.

“Will you not fear me?” says the Lord. “Will you not tremble before me? I set the sand as a boundary for the sea, an everlasting decree that it cannot cross. It struggles but cannot prevail; its waves rise up but cannot cross it.”
But this people has a rebellious and defiant heart. They have turned aside and gone away.
They did not say in their hearts, “Let us fear the Lord our God, who gives the early and late rain in its season and preserves the summer crops for us for the winter.”
Your offenses have brought these things upon you, and your sins have kept good things from you.
For sinners have been found among my people. They have set up snares like fences, so that people may be caught in them.
Like a cage full of birds, their houses are full of deceit. This is why they have become great and wealthy.
They have overstepped justice. They have not judged fairly, have not upheld the case of orphans, and have not judged the case of the poor.
Shall I not punish them for these things, says the LORD? Shall I not take vengeance on a people like this?
An astonishing and foolish thing has happened in the land.
The prophets prophesied lies, and the priests joined hands with them. My people loved it that way. But what will you do in the end?
Flee from within Jerusalem, people of Benjamin! Sound the trumpet loudly, and raise a signal over Beth-haccherem, for I am bringing disaster from the north and great destruction.
I have compared daughter Zion to a delicate, pampered woman.
Shepherds and their flocks will come against her together. They will pitch their tents all around her, and each will graze his flock in his own place.
Prepare for war against her! They will say, “Come, let us go up at noon! Alas for us, for the day is declining and the evening shadows are stretching out!”
Come, let us go up against her at night and destroy her strongholds!
For this is what the mighty Lord says: “Cut down her trees and set ambushes against Jerusalem. This is the city marked for punishment; it is full of oppression.”
As a cistern gathers its water, so she has gathered her wickedness. Violence and plunder are heard within her; pain and wounds are continually before me.
Accept correction, Jerusalem, lest I turn away from you, lest I make you a wasteland, like an uninhabited land.
This is what the mighty Lord says: “They will thoroughly glean the remnant of Israel like a vine. Pass your hand over the gleanings again, like a grape picker.”

To whom can I speak and give warning so that they will listen? Look, their ears are uncircumcised, and they cannot listen. Look, the word of the Lord has become an object of scorn to them, and they take no pleasure in it.

And you are filled with the Lord’s wrath and have grown weary of holding it in. Pour it out on the children in the streets and on the gatherings of young men together, for men and women alike will be seized, the old along with those young in years.
Their houses will be given to others, together with their fields and wives, for I am raising my hand against the inhabitants of the land, says the Lord.
For from the least of them to the greatest, they all practice deceit; from the false prophets to the priests, they all act falsely.
They treat the wound of the daughter of my people with mockery, saying, “Peace, peace,” when there is no peace.

They were put to shame because they committed abominations, yet they feel no shame and do not know how to blush. Therefore they will fall among the fallen; when they are called to account, they will be overthrown, says the Lord.

This is what the Lord says: “Stand at the roads and look. Ask about the ancient paths, and see which is the good way. Walk in it and find rest for yourselves.” But they said, “We will not walk in it.”
I appointed watchmen over you so that you would listen to the sound of the trumpet. But you say, 'We will not listen.'
Therefore hear, nations, and know, assembly, what is among them.
Listen, earth! Look, I am bringing disaster on this people as the fruit of their schemes, because they have not listened to my words and have rejected my law.
What use to me is the frankincense you bring from Sheba, or the fragrant cane from a distant land? I do not want your burnt offerings, and your sacrifices do not please me.
Therefore this is what the Lord says: Look, I am placing stumbling blocks before this people. Fathers and children together will stumble over them; neighbors and their friends will perish.
This is what the Lord says: Look, a people is coming from the northern land, and a great nation will rise from the ends of the earth.
They are armed with bows and spears. They are cruel and show no mercy. Their sound is like a raging sea. They ride horses and are prepared like warriors for battle against you, daughter Zion.
We have heard the news of them, and our hands have grown weak. Distress has seized us, and pains like those of a woman giving birth.
Do not go out into the field or walk along the road, because the sword of the enemies surrounds you.
Daughter of my people, wrap yourself in sackcloth and roll in ashes. Mourn as for an only child, and wail bitterly, because plunderers will suddenly come upon you.
I have appointed you as a strong tester among my people, so that you may know and examine their ways.
All their rulers are rebellious and act deceitfully. They are like bronze and iron; all of them act corruptly.
The bellows are worn out by their fire and lead. The refiner refines in vain, and their wickedness does not come to an end.
They are called rejected silver, because the Lord has rejected them.
The word that came to Jeremiah from the Lord, saying:
Stand at the gate of the Lord’s house and proclaim this message there. Say: Hear the word of the Lord, all you of the house of Judah who enter these gates to worship the Lord.
This is what the Lord Almighty, the God of Israel, says: Make your ways and your deeds good, and I will let you live in this place.
Do not trust the lying words of those who say to you, ‘The temple of the Lord, the temple of the Lord! You are the temple of the Lord!’
If you improve your ways and your deeds, and if you administer justice between one person and another,
Do not mistreat or oppress foreign residents, orphans, or widows. Do not shed innocent blood in this place, and do not follow other gods, bringing harm upon yourselves.
then I will let you live in this place, in the land that I gave your ancestors, forever and ever.
But look, you are trusting in lying words that are of no use.
You steal, murder, commit adultery, swear falsely by my name, burn incense to Baal, and follow other gods whom you have not known.
Then you come and stand before me in this house that bears my name and say, ‘Save us!’ Yet you do all these evil things.
Has this house that bears my name become a den of thieves in your eyes? Look, I too have seen it, says the Lord.
Therefore go to my place in Shiloh, where I first made my name dwell, and see what I did to it because of the wickedness of my people Israel.
And now, because you have done all these things, says the Lord, and I spoke to you early, but you did not listen, and I called to you, but you did not answer,
I will do to this house that bears my name, in which you trust, and to the town that I gave to you and your ancestors, just as I did to Shiloh.
I will cast you out of my presence, just as I cast out all your brothers, all the descendants of Ephraim.
As for you, do not pray for this people. Do not plead on their behalf or make requests of me, because I will not listen to you.
Do you not see what they are doing in the towns of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem?
The children gather wood, the fathers light the fire, and the women knead dough to make cakes for the worship of heaven and to pour out drink offerings to other gods, provoking me to anger.
“It is not me they provoke to anger,” says the Lord, “but themselves, bringing shame on their own faces.”

Therefore this is what the Lord God says: Look, my anger and my fury are settling upon this place, upon people and animals, upon the trees of the field and the fruit of the ground. It will burn and will not be extinguished.
This is what the Lord Almighty, the God of Israel, says: Add their burnt offerings to their sacrifices, and eat meat.
For when I brought their ancestors up from the land of Egypt, I did not speak to them or command them concerning burnt offerings or sacrifices.
Instead, this is what I commanded them: Listen to my voice, and I will be your God, and you will be my people. Walk in every way that I command you, so that things may go well for you.
But they did not listen or incline their ears to hear. Instead, they followed their own thoughts and the desires of their evil hearts. They turned backward rather than forward.
From the day their ancestors came out of the land of Egypt until today, I have sent all my servants the prophets to them, sending them early every day.
But they did not listen or incline their ears to me. They stiffened their necks more than their ancestors did.
You will tell them all these words, but they will not listen to you. You will call to them, but they will not answer you.
Faithfulness has perished and has been cut off from their mouths.
Cut off your hair and throw it away. Raise a lament along the paths, for the Lord is angry and has abandoned the rebellious generation.
For the people of Judah have done evil in my sight, says the Lord. They have put their filthy idols in the house that bears my name and have defiled it.
They built high places at Topheth, in the Valley of Ben-hinnom, to burn their sons and daughters in the fire—something I did not command them and that never entered my mind.

Therefore, look, the days are coming, says the Lord, when it will no longer be called Topheth or the Valley of Ben-hinnom, but the Valley of the Slain. They will bury people in Topheth because there is no other place.
The corpses of this people will become food for the birds of the sky and the animals of the earth, and there will be no one to rescue them.

I will put an end to the sound of rejoicing and the sound of gladness, the voice of the bridegroom and the voice of the bride, in the towns of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem, because the whole land will become a wasteland.

At that time, says the Lord, they will bring the bones of the kings of Judah, the bones of their officials, the bones of their priests, the bones of their prophets, and the bones of the inhabitants of Jerusalem out of their graves.

They will spread them out before the sun, the moon, and all the heavenly bodies, which they loved, served, followed, consulted, and worshiped. Their bones will not be gathered or buried, but will lie like dung on the ground.
All who remain of this evil generation will choose death rather than life, in every place where I have scattered them, says the Lord Almighty.
You shall tell them: This is what the Lord says: “Do people fall and not get up? And if they turn away, do they not return?
Why has this people, Jerusalem, turned away so shamelessly? They cling to deceit and refuse to return.
I listened and heard, but they were not speaking honestly. No one regrets his evil or says, ‘What have I done?’ They all follow their own will, like a horse charging into battle.
Even the stork in the sky knows her season, and the turtledove, the crane, and the swallow observe the time of their arrival. But my people do not know the Lord’s judgment.
How can you say, ‘We are wise, and the Lord’s law is with us’? Surely the scribe’s lying pen has turned it into a lie.
The wise have been put to shame; they have been shattered and captured. Because they rejected the word of the Lord, there is no wisdom in them.

Therefore I will give their wives to others and their fields as plunder, because from the least to the greatest, they all practice deceit. From the false prophets to the priests, they all act falsely.
They treat the wound of the daughter of my people with contempt, saying, “Peace, peace,” when there is no peace.

They were put to shame because they committed vile acts, yet they feel no shame and do not know how to blush. Therefore they will fall among the fallen, and when they are called to account, they will be overthrown, says the Lord.
I will completely sweep them away, says the Lord. There are no grapes on the vine and no figs on the fig tree, and the leaves have fallen. I gave to them, but they passed them by.

They will say, ‘Why are we sitting here? Gather together, and let us enter the fortified towns and be silent there, because the Lord our God has silenced us and given us bitter water to drink, because we have sinned against the Lord.’
We waited for peace, but nothing good came; for a time of healing, but distress came upon us.
The neighing of his horses was heard from Dan. At the sound of his warriors’ cries, the whole land trembled. They came and devoured the land and everything in it, the city and its inhabitants.
For look, I am sending snakes among you, vipers that will not respond to charms, and they will bite you, says the Lord.
I am worn out in my distress, and my heart is sick within me.

Listen to the cry of the daughter of my people from a distant land! They say, ‘Is the Lord not in Zion? Is her king not within her?’ For they have angered me with their carved images and foreign idols.
The harvest has passed, the fruit gathering has ended, and we have not been saved.
I grieve over the wound of the daughter of my people, and horror has seized me.
Is there no balm in Gilead? Is there no physician there? Why, then, has healing not come to the daughter of my people?
If only someone would make my head water and my eyes fountains of tears, so that I could weep day and night for the slain of the daughter of my people!
If only someone would leave me a travelers’ lodging in the wilderness, so that I could leave my people and go away from them! For they are all adulterers, a gathering of liars.

They shoot with their tongues as with their bows. Through falsehood, not faithfulness, they have grown strong in the land. For they go from one evil to another, and they do not know me, says the Lord.
Let each of you beware of his neighbor, and do not trust any brother, because every brother practices deceit, and every friend walks in deceit.
They lie to one another and do not speak the truth. They have taught their tongues to speak lies, and they have worn themselves out and grown weary.
You dwell in the midst of deceit. In their deceit they refused to know me, says the Lord.
Therefore this is what the Lord Almighty says: Look, I will refine them and test them. For what else can I do because of the daughter of my people?
Their tongue is like a sharpened arrow and speaks deceit. Each speaks peace to his neighbor with his mouth, but inwardly he lays an ambush.
Shall I not punish them for these things, says the Lord? Shall I not take vengeance on a people like this?

Raise weeping and lamentation over the mountains, and a lament over the pastures of the wilderness, because they are desolate, with no one passing through. The sound of livestock is not heard. From the birds of the sky to the animals, they have scattered and gone.
I will make Jerusalem a ruin, a dwelling for jackals, and I will turn the towns of Judah into a wasteland, with no one living there.

Who is wise enough to understand this? To whom has the word from the LORD’s mouth come, so that he can explain it? Why has the land perished and become desolate like a wilderness, with no one passing through?
The LORD said, “Because they abandoned my law, which I gave to them and their ancestors, and did not listen to my voice or follow it.”
Instead, they followed the desires of their evil hearts and the idols their ancestors taught them to follow.”
Therefore this is what the LORD Almighty, the God of Israel, says: “Look, I will feed this people bitter herbs and give them bitter water to drink.
I will scatter them among nations that neither they nor their ancestors have known, and I will send the sword after them until I have destroyed them.”
This is what the Lord Almighty says: Call for the mourning women, and let them come. Send for the skilled women, and let them come.
Let them hurry and raise a lament over us, so that our eyes shed tears and our pupils stream with water.
For a sound of lamentation is heard from Zion, saying, “How we have been plundered! We are utterly ashamed, because we have left the land and our dwellings have fallen.”
Therefore, women, hear the word of the LORD. Let your ears receive the word of his mouth. Teach your daughters laments, and let each woman teach her neighbor a song of mourning.
For death has climbed through our windows and entered our palaces, to destroy the children in the streets and the young men in the public squares.
For this is what the LORD says: “Human corpses will fall like manure on the surface of the field, like cut grain behind the reaper, with no one to gather it.”
This is what the LORD says: “Let the wise not boast in their wisdom, the mighty not boast in their might, and the rich not boast in their riches.

Instead, let anyone who boasts boast in this: that they understand and know me, that I am the LORD, who acts with kindness, justice, and righteousness on the earth. For I delight in these things,” says the LORD.
Look, the days are coming, says the Lord, when I will punish all who are circumcised but remain uncircumcised:

Against the Egyptians, the Jews, Edom, the Ammonites, Moab, and all who clip the hair at their temples and live in the wilderness. For all the nations are uncircumcised in their flesh, and all the house of Israel are uncircumcised in their hearts.
Hear the word that the Lord speaks against you, house of Israel.
This is what the LORD says: “Do not learn the ways of the nations, and do not be afraid of signs in the heavens, for it is the nations that are afraid of them.
For the nations’ objects of worship are nothing: wood cut from the forest, the work of a carpenter’s hands with an axe.
They are covered with silver and gold. They fasten them with hammers and nails so that they will not come apart.
They stand upright like palm trees but cannot speak. They must be carried because they cannot walk. Do not be afraid of them, for they can do neither harm nor good.”
There is no one like you, Lord. You are great, and your name is great in might.
Who would not fear you, King of all ages? For kingship belongs to you. Among all the wise people of the nations and throughout all their kingdoms, there is no one like you.
Together they will perish and come to an end—the worthless teachings of wooden idols.
Fine silver comes from Tarshish, and gold from Ophir, the work of a carpenter and the hands of a metalworker. Their clothing is blue and purple, woven by skilled workers.
But the LORD is the true God. He is the living God and the eternal King. The earth trembles at his anger, and the nations cannot endure his wrath.
Say this to them: “The gods that did not make the heavens and the earth will perish from the earth and from beneath these heavens.”
The Lord made the earth by his power, established the world by his wisdom, and stretched out the heavens by his understanding.
He makes the waters roar in the heavens. He raises clouds from the ends of the earth, makes lightning for the rain, and brings winds out of his storehouses.
Everyone is foolish and without knowledge. All goldsmiths are put to shame by the carved images they have made, for they have cast a lie, and there is no breath in them.
They are nothing, works of folly. When the time comes for their punishment, they will perish.
Jacob’s portion is not like these, for the one who created everything is their portion, and Israel is the tribe of his inheritance. The LORD Almighty is his name.
Gather up your shame from the land, you who live in distress.
For this is what the LORD says: “Look, at this time I am bringing distress on the inhabitants of this land, so that they will seek me and find me.”
Woe to me because of my brokenness! My wound is painful. But I said, “This is my suffering, and I will bear it.”
My tent has been plundered, and all its ropes have been cut. My children have left me and are no more. There is no one to pitch my tent again or put up my tent curtains.
For the shepherds have become foolish and have not sought the Lord. Because they have not prospered, their whole flock has been scattered.
Listen! A report is coming, and a great uproar from the northern land, to turn the towns of Judah into ruins, a dwelling place for jackals.
I know that the Lord’s ways are not like those of a human being, nor like those of a man who goes along arranging his affairs.
Discipline me, Lord, with justice, not in your anger, lest you reduce me to nothing.

Pour out your wrath on the nations that do not know you and on the families that do not call on your name. For they have devoured Jacob; they have devoured him and finished him off, and they have laid waste his dwelling place.
The word that came to Jeremiah from the Lord, saying:
Hear the words of this covenant, and speak to the men of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
Tell them: This is what the Lord Almighty, the God of Israel, says: Cursed is the person who does not obey the words of this covenant,

which I commanded your ancestors on the day I brought them out of the land of Egypt, out of the iron furnace. I said, ‘Listen to my voice and do everything I command you. You will be my people, and I will be your God,
and I will fulfill the oaths I swore to your ancestors, to give you a land flowing with milk and honey, as it is today.’ Then I answered, ‘Amen, Lord.’
The Lord said to me, ‘Proclaim all these words in the towns of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem. Say, “Listen to the words of this covenant and carry them out.
For I solemnly warned your ancestors on the day I brought them up out of the land of Egypt, and down to this day I have risen early and sent word, saying, ‘Listen to my voice.’

But they did not listen or incline their ears. Each followed the desires of their evil heart. So I brought upon them all the words of this covenant, which I commanded them to obey, but they did not obey.”’
The Lord said to me: Rebellion has been found among the men of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem.

They have returned to the sins of their ancestors of old and have refused to listen to my words. They have gone after other gods to serve them. The people of Israel and the people of Judah have broken my covenant, which I established with their ancestors.
Therefore this is what the Lord Almighty says: Look, I am bringing disaster upon them from which they cannot escape. They will cry out to me, but I will not listen to them.
Then the towns of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem will go and cry out to the gods to whom they used to offer incense, but those gods will certainly not save them in the time of their disaster.
For your gods have become as numerous as your towns, Judah. You have set up as many altars to shame as there are streets in Jerusalem—altars for offering incense to Baal.
As for you, do not pray for this people or offer a petition or prayer on their behalf, for I will not listen when they call to me in the time of their disaster.
Why, my beloved, have you done so many filthy things in my house? The holy meat will be taken away from you because your wickedness has grown great.
The Lord called you a flourishing olive tree, beautiful in fruit and beautiful in appearance. At the sound of a great decree, set fire to it, and its branches will be destroyed.

The Lord of hosts, who planted you, has pronounced disaster against you because of the evil that the house of Israel and the house of Judah have done to themselves, provoking me to anger by offering incense to Baal.
Lord, show me, and I will know. Truly, you have shown me their deeds.

I was like an innocent lamb being led to slaughter, and I did not know that they had plotted against me, saying, ‘Let us destroy the tree with its fruit. Let us wipe him out from the land of the living, so that his name will no longer be remembered.’
But you, Lord Almighty, are a righteous judge who examines the innermost thoughts and the heart. Let me see your vengeance upon them, for I have laid my case before you.
Therefore this is what the Lord says about the men of Anathoth who seek your life and say, ‘Do not prophesy in the Lord’s name, or you will die at our hands.’
Therefore this is what the Lord of hosts says: Look, I will punish them. Their young men will die by the sword, and their sons and daughters will die of famine.
They will have no survivors, because I will bring disaster on the people of Anathoth in the year of their punishment.”
You are righteous, Lord, when I bring a case against you. Yet I will speak to you about justice: Why does the way of the wicked prosper? Why do all the deceitful live at ease?
You planted them, and they became established; they took root and even bore fruit. You are near in their mouths but far from their innermost thoughts.
But you, Lord, know me and have seen me, and you have examined my heart before you. Prepare them like sheep for slaughter, and appoint them for the day of killing.
How long will the land mourn and all the grass of the fields wither? Because of the wickedness of its inhabitants, the animals and birds have perished, for they said, ‘He will not see our end.’
Look, you ran with men on foot, and they wore you out. How will you compete with horses? You feel secure in a peaceful land, but how will you pass through the raging Jordan?
For even your brothers and your father's household have betrayed you; even they have spoken against you behind your back. Do not trust them when they speak kindly to you.
I have abandoned my house; I have abandoned my inheritance. I have handed the one I dearly love over to her enemies.
My inheritance has become to me like a lion in the forest. She has raised her voice against me; therefore I hate her.
My inheritance has become like a speckled bird to me, with birds surrounding it. Go, gather all the wild animals; bring them to devour it.
Many shepherds have ruined my vineyard and trampled my portion. They have turned my cherished portion into a desolate wilderness.
They have laid it waste and devastated it. Desolate, it mourns before me. The whole land has become desolate because no one takes it to heart.
Plunderers have come along all the paths of the wilderness, for the LORD's sword devours from one end of the land to the other. No one has peace.
Sow wheat and reap thorns! Wear yourselves out, but you gain nothing. Be ashamed of your harvests because of the fierce anger of the LORD.

This is what the LORD says about all my evil neighbors who have encroached on the inheritance I gave my people Israel: Look, I am uprooting them from their land, and I will uproot the house of Judah from among them.
After I uproot them, I will again have compassion on them and bring them back, each to his inheritance and each to his land.
If they teach my ways to my people, to swear by my name, 'As the LORD lives,' just as they taught my people to swear by Baal, they will settle among my people.
But if they will not listen, I will utterly uproot and destroy that nation,” says the Lord.
This is what the LORD said to me: Go, buy yourself a linen loincloth and tie it around your waist, but do not dip it in water.
So I bought a sash according to the Lord’s word and tied it around my waist.
The word of the Lord came to me a second time, saying:
“Take the sash you bought, which is around your waist, and get up and go to the Euphrates. Hide it there in a crevice in the rock.”
So I went and hid it by the Euphrates, as the Lord had commanded me.
After many days, the LORD said to me: Get up, go to the Euphrates, and take from there the loincloth that I commanded you to hide there.
I went to the Euphrates, dug, and took the loincloth from the place where I had hidden it. And there was the loincloth, ruined and good for nothing.
The word of the Lord came to me, saying:
This is what the LORD Almighty, the God of Israel, says: In this same way I will ruin the proud people of Judah and the many proud people of Jerusalem.

These evil people, who refused to listen to my words, who follow the desires of their own hearts and have gone after other gods to serve and worship them, will become like this loincloth, which is good for nothing.

For just as a loincloth clings to a man's waist, so I made the whole house of Israel and the whole house of Judah cling to me, says the LORD, so that they might be my people, my name, my honor, and my praise. But they did not listen.

Tell them this message: This is what the LORD Almighty, the God of Israel, says: Every wineskin will be filled with wine. Look, they will say to you, 'Do we not know perfectly well that all wineskins are filled with wine?'

Tell them: This is what the LORD says: Look, I am filling all the inhabitants of this land with drunkenness—the kings who sit on David's throne, the priests, the prophets, and all the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
I will scatter them away from one another, fathers and children alike, says the LORD. I will show no compassion, no mercy, and no pity to keep me from destroying them.
Listen and pay attention. Do not be proud, for the Lord has spoken.

Give honor to the LORD your God before he brings darkness, before your feet are broken on the mountains in the darkness. You will wait for light, but he will turn it into darkness and the shadows of death.
If you do not listen to him, my soul will weep in secret because of distress. I will weep bitterly, and my eyes will stream with tears because the LORD's flock has been taken captive.
Tell the kings and the rulers: Humble yourselves and sit down, for your glorious crown has fallen from your heads.
The towns of the south have been shut, and there is no one to open them. All Judah has been taken captive, carried away completely.
Lift up your eyes and see those coming from the north. Where is the flock that was given to you, the sheep that were your glory?
What will you say when he punishes you? You yourself trained them to trample. Look, pains will seize you like a woman in labor giving birth.
If you say in your heart, 'Why have these things happened to me?' it is because of your many sins that your skirts have been rolled up and your heels exposed.
Just as an Indian cannot change his skin or a leopard its spots, neither can you do good, because you have become accustomed to evil.
I will scatter them like chaff passing before the wind in the wilderness.
This is your lot and your allotted inheritance from me, says the Lord, because you have forgotten me and trusted in falsehood.
I myself will lift your skirts and throw them over your face, and your shame will be seen.

Your adultery, your neighing, and the lewdness of your prostitution—on the heights in the wilderness I have seen your defilement. Woe to you, Jerusalem! You will not be cleansed. How long before you turn back?
The word of the Lord came to Jeremiah concerning the lack of rain.
Judah mourned, and her gates became desolate and fell to the ground. Jerusalem’s cry went up.
Their nobles sent their servants for water. They came to the cisterns and found no water. They brought their vessels back empty. They were ashamed and humiliated and covered their heads.
Because of the deeds of the land, there was no rain. The farmers were ashamed and covered their heads.
Even the does in the open country gave birth and abandoned their young because there was no fresh grass.
The wild donkeys stood on the paths, panting for air like jackals. Their eyes grew dim because there was no grass.
Even if our sins testify against us, Lord, have pity for your name’s sake, because your kindness is great, and we have sinned against you.
Hope of Israel and its Savior in a time of distress, do not be like a stranger in the land, like a traveler who turns aside to spend the night.
Do not be like a weak man, like a man who cannot save. You, Lord, are among us, and your name has been called over us. Do not abandon us.

This is what the Lord says to this people: They have loved to wander and have not restrained their feet. The Lord takes no pleasure in them. Now he will remember their wrongdoing and punish their sins.
The Lord said to me, “Do not pray for the welfare of this people.”
For even if they fast, I will not hear their prayer, and even if they offer burnt offerings and sacrifices, I will not accept them. For I will finish them off with sword, famine, and pestilence.
Then I said, “Please, Lord God! Look, the prophets are telling them, ‘You will not see the sword, and you will not suffer famine. Instead, I will give you peace and truth in this place.’”

The Lord said to me, “The prophets are prophesying lies in my name. I did not send them, command them, or speak to them. They are prophesying to you false visions, divination, omens, and the deceit of their own hearts.”

Therefore this is what the Lord says about the prophets who prophesy in my name, though I did not send them, and who say, “There will be no sword or famine in this land”: Those prophets will perish by sword and famine.

The people to whom they prophesy will lie thrown into the streets of Jerusalem because of sword, famine, and pestilence. There will be no one to bury them, their wives, their sons, or their daughters. I will pour their own wickedness down upon them.
Say this word to them: Let my eyes stream with tears day and night, and let them not stop, because the virgin daughter of my people has suffered a great crushing blow, a very painful wound.

If I go out into the countryside, there are those killed by the sword! If I enter the city, there are those wasted by famine! For both prophets and priests have wandered through the land without understanding.

Have you utterly rejected Judah? Do you loathe Zion? Why have you struck us so that there is no healing for us? We waited for peace, but nothing good came; for a time of healing, but there was terror!
We acknowledge our sins, Lord, and the sins of our ancestors, for we have sinned against you.
For your name’s sake, do not be angry, and do not dishonor your glorious throne. Remember, and do not break your covenant with us.
For the idols of the nations cannot bring down rain, nor can the heavens give showers. Rather, it is you, Lord our God. We will wait for you, for you do all these things.
The Lord said to me, “Even if Moses and Samuel stood before me, I would take no pleasure in this people. Send them out of my presence, and let them go.”

If they say to you, “Where shall we go?” tell them: This is what the Lord says: Those destined for death, to death; those destined for the sword, to the sword; those destined for famine, to famine; and those destined for captivity, to captivity.
I will appoint four scourges over them, says the Lord: the sword to kill, dogs to drag away, and the birds of the sky and the animals of the earth to devour and destroy.
I will make them an object of horror among all the kingdoms of the earth because of the sins of Manasseh son of Hezekiah, king of Judah, because of everything he did in Jerusalem.
Who will pity you, Jerusalem? Who will grieve for you? Who will turn aside to ask how you are?
You have abandoned me, says the Lord, and have gone backward. I will raise my hand against you and destroy you, and I will no longer spare them.
“I will winnow them with a winnowing fork in the towns of the land. I have bereaved and destroyed my people, yet they have not turned from their ways.”
Their widows have become more numerous than the sand of the sea. I brought plunderers against them, against mothers and young men, at noon. Suddenly I cast turmoil and trembling upon them.

The woman who bore seven has grown weak; her belly has swollen. Her sun has set in the middle of her days. She is ashamed and humiliated. I will hand over those who remain to the sword before their enemies, says the Lord.
Woe to me, my mother, that you bore me, a man of contention and a man of rebuke throughout the whole land! I owe no one anything, and no one owes me anything, yet they all insult me.
The Lord said, “I will not leave you in prosperity. Instead, I will bring an enemy from the north against you in a time of distress, in a time of disaster.”
“who is hard as iron and bronze.”
“I will give your possessions, your treasures, and all your territory as plunder because of your sins.”
I will enslave you to your enemies in a land you do not know, for a fire has been kindled in my anger; it will burn against you.
You know, LORD. Remember me and save me, and avenge me on my persecutors. Do not take me away while you are patient with them. Know that I have endured disgrace for your sake.
I have kept your commandments and carried them out, and your word became a delight to me and the joy of my heart, because your name is called over me, LORD, mighty God.
I did not sit in the company of mockers. Instead, I feared your hand and sat alone, because you filled me with anger.
Why has my pain become severe, and my wound grievous, refusing to heal? You have become to me like deceptive waters that cannot be trusted.

Therefore this is what the LORD says: If you return, I will restore you, and you will stand before me. If you bring out what is precious from what is worthless, you will be like my mouth. Let them turn to you, but you must not turn to them.
I have made you like a strong bronze wall against this people. They will fight against you, but they will not overcome you, because I am with you to save you and rescue you, says the LORD.
I will deliver you from the hand of the wicked and rescue you from the hand of the powerful.
The word of the Lord came to me, saying:
Do not take a wife, and do not have sons or daughters in this place.
For this is what the LORD says about the sons and daughters born in this place, about their mothers who bear them, and about their fathers who father them in this place:

They will die the death of those wasted by famine. No one will mourn for them, and they will not be buried. Instead, they will be like manure on the ground. They will perish by the sword and by famine, and their corpses will become food for the birds of the sky and the animals of the earth.

For this is what the LORD says: Do not enter a house of mourning, and do not go to mourn or grieve for them, because I have withdrawn my peace from this people, says the LORD, along with kindness and mercy.
Both great and small will die in this land. They will not be buried, and no one will mourn for them or wail or shave their heads for them.
No one will break bread for them in mourning to comfort them over the dead, nor will anyone give them the cup of consolation to drink for their fathers or their mothers.
Do not enter a house of feasting to sit with them, to eat and drink.

For this is what the LORD, the mighty God of Israel, says: Look, in your sight and in your own days, I am putting an end in this place to the sound of rejoicing and the sound of gladness, the voice of the bridegroom and the voice of the bride.

When you tell this people all these words, they will say to you, 'Why has the LORD pronounced all this great disaster against us? What wrong have we done? What is our sin that we have committed against the LORD our God?'
Tell them: Because your ancestors abandoned me, says the LORD, and followed other gods, served them, and bowed down to them. They abandoned me and did not keep my law.
You have acted even more wickedly than your ancestors. Look, each of you follows the desires of your evil hearts, refusing to listen to me.
I will throw you out of this land into a land that neither you nor your ancestors have known. There you will serve other gods day and night, and I will show you no mercy.
Therefore, look, the days are coming, says the LORD, when people will no longer say, 'As the LORD lives, who brought the house of Israel up from the land of Egypt,'

but rather, 'As the LORD lives, who will bring the house of Israel up and lead them from the northern land and from all the countries where I drove them.' I will bring them back to their own land, which I gave to their ancestors.

Look, I am sending for many fishermen, says the LORD, and they will catch them. Afterward I will send for many hunters, and they will hunt them from every mountain, from every hill, and from the crevices of the cliffs.
For my eyes are on all their ways. They are not hidden from me, and their wrongdoing is not concealed from my eyes.
First I will repay them double for their offenses and their sins, because they have defiled my land with sacrifices to their idols and filled my inheritance with their filth.

LORD, my strength, my helper, and my refuge in the day of distress, the nations will come to you from the ends of the earth and say, 'Truly, the false idols our ancestors handed down to us are nothing, and there is no benefit in them.'
Look, human beings make gods for themselves, but they are not gods.
Therefore, look, I am showing them; this time I will make them know my hand and my might, and they will know that my name is the LORD.
Judah's sin is written with an iron pen and a diamond point, engraved on the tablets of their hearts and on the horns of their altars.
When they remember in their hearts their altars and the objects of their worship beneath every leafy tree and on every high hill.
in the mountains and in the open country, I will give your property, all your treasures, and your territories as plunder because of your sins.
I will remove you from the inheritance I gave you and make you serve your enemies in a land you do not know, because you have kindled a fire in my anger that will burn forever.
This is what the Lord says: Cursed is the man who trusts in a human being, makes mortal flesh his strength, and turns his heart away from the Lord.
He will be like a stump in the plain and will not see good when it comes. He will live in sandy places in the wilderness, in an uninhabited salt land.
Blessed is the person who trusts in the LORD, whose confidence is the LORD.

He will be like a tree planted beside water, with its roots firmly established beside a stream. It will not fear when heat comes, and its leaves will flourish. In a year with little rain it will not fear, nor will it stop bearing fruit.
The heart is stronger than everything; it is human. Who knows it?
I, the Lord, search the heart and examine the innermost thoughts, giving each person according to his ways and according to the fruit of his deeds.
Like a partridge that calls to young it did not hatch, so is someone who acquires wealth unjustly. In the middle of his days it will leave him, and his end will be shameful.
A glorious throne, exalted from the beginning, from the place of our sanctuary.
The Lord is the hope of Israel. All who abandon you will be put to shame, and rebels will be written in the earth, because they have abandoned the Lord, the spring of living water.
Heal me, LORD, and I will be healed. Save me, and I will be saved, for you are my praise.
Look, they say to me, “Where is the LORD’s word? Let it come now!”
As for me, I did not draw back from you in adversity. You know that I did not long for the day of man, and whatever came from my lips was before you.
Do not bring ruin upon me, but shelter me on the day of trouble.

Let my persecutors be put to shame, but do not let me be put to shame. Let them be shattered, but do not let me be shattered. Bring a day of disaster upon them, and shatter them with double destruction.
This is what the Lord said to me: Go and stand at the gate of the common people, through which the kings of Judah enter and leave, and at all the gates of Jerusalem.
Say to them: Hear the word of the Lord, kings of Judah, all the house of Judah, and all the inhabitants of Jerusalem who enter through these gates.
This is what the Lord says: Take care for your lives. Do not carry a load on the Sabbath day and bring it through the gates of Jerusalem.
Do not bring a load out of your houses on the Sabbath day, and do not do any work. Keep the Sabbath day holy, as I commanded your ancestors.
But they did not listen or turn their ears to hear. They stiffened their necks so that they would neither listen nor accept correction.
But if you truly listen to me, says the Lord, bringing no load through the gates of this city on the Sabbath day, keeping the Sabbath day holy, and doing no work on it,

then kings and officials who sit on David’s throne will enter through the gates of this city, riding in chariots and on horses—they and their officials, the men of Judah, and the inhabitants of Jerusalem. This city will be inhabited forever.

They will come from the towns of Judah, from the places around Jerusalem, from the land of Benjamin, from the plain, from the hill country, and from the south, bringing sacrifices, offerings, and frankincense, and bringing thanksgiving offerings to the house of the Lord.

But if you do not listen to me and keep the Sabbath day holy by carrying no load through the gates of Jerusalem on the Sabbath day, I will set fire to its gates. It will consume Jerusalem’s palaces and will not be extinguished.
The word that came to Jeremiah from the Lord, saying:
Get up and go down to the potter’s house, and there I will let you hear my words.
So I went down to the potter’s house, as the Lord had instructed, and there he was, working at the wheel.
The clay vessel that the potter was making was spoiled in his hand, so he made it again into another vessel, as he wished.
The word of the Lord came to me, saying:
Can I not do to you as this potter does, house of Israel? says the Lord. Look, as clay is in the potter’s hands, so you are in my hands, house of Israel.
If I suddenly declare concerning a nation or a kingdom that I will uproot, tear down, overthrow, and destroy it,
and that nation turns from its wickedness, I will turn away from it the disaster I had planned to bring upon it.
And if I declare concerning a nation or a kingdom that I will build and plant it,
and it does what is evil in my sight and does not obey my voice, I will withhold from it the good that I said I would do for it.

Now say to the men of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem: This is what the Lord says: Look, I am shaping disaster against you and devising a plan against you. Return! Turn back, each of you, from your evil way, and make your ways and deeds good.
But they said, “We will stand firm and follow our own plans, and each of us will carry out the desires of his evil heart.”
Therefore this is what the Lord says: Ask among the nations: Who has done such things? Virgin Israel has committed great folly.
Does snow disappear from the mountain’s breasts and from Lebanon? Do the cold waters flowing from foreign lands stop?
For my people have forgotten me and burned incense to worthless things. They have stumbled in their ways, on the ancient paths, to walk along trails, on a road that has not been cleared.
making their land an object of horror and of hissing forever. Everyone who passes through it will be appalled and shake his head.
Like a scorching wind I will scatter them before their enemies. I will show them my back and not my face on the day of their distress.

They said, “Come, let us devise a plot against Jeremiah, for instruction will not disappear from the priests, nor counsel from the wise, nor the word from the prophets. Come, let us strike him on the tongue and pay no attention to anything he says.”
Listen to me, Lord, and hear how I am insulted.
Is evil repaid for good? For they have dug a pit for my life. Remember that I stood before you and spoke well of them, to turn your anger away from them.

Therefore, give their children over to famine and hand them over to the power of the sword. Let their wives be childless and widowed. Let their men be struck down by death, and their young men be killed by the sword in battle.
Let wailing be heard from their houses when you suddenly bring a raiding force against them, because they dug a pit to trap me and hid snares for my feet.

But you, LORD, know everything they have plotted to put me to death. Do not forgive their wrongdoing or wipe away their sins from before you. Let them lie fallen before you; pass through them in the time of your anger.
This is what the LORD said to me: “Go and buy an earthenware jug, and take with you some of the elders of the people and some of the elders of the priests.”
Go out to the Valley of Ben Hinnom, at the entrance of the Gate of [?], and proclaim there the words that I tell you.

“Say, ‘Hear the word of the LORD, kings of Judah and inhabitants of Jerusalem. This is what the LORD Almighty, the God of Israel, says: Look, I am bringing disaster on this place, so that the ears of everyone who hears about it will ring.

They have abandoned me and defiled this place. They have burned incense here to other gods, gods unknown to them, their ancestors, and the kings of Judah. They have filled this place with innocent blood.
They filled [?] the high places for Baal, to burn their children in the fire as burnt offerings to Baal—something I neither commanded nor spoke of, nor did it enter my mind.
Therefore, look, the days are coming, says the LORD, when this place will no longer be called Topheth or the Valley of Ben Hinnom, but the Valley of the Slain.

I will frustrate the plans of Judah and Jerusalem in this place. I will make them fall by the sword before their enemies, at the hands of those seeking their lives. I will give their corpses as food to the birds of the sky and the animals of the earth.
I will make this city an object of horror and hissing. Everyone who passes by it will be horrified and hiss at all its wounds.
I will make them eat the flesh of their sons and daughters. Each will eat the flesh of his neighbor in the distress and hardship inflicted on them by their enemies and those seeking their lives.’”
Break the jar in full view of the men who go with you.

“Say to them, ‘This is what the LORD Almighty says: In this way I will break this people and this city, just as this earthenware vessel is broken and can never be repaired. They will bury people in Topheth because there is no other place to bury them.
This is what I will do to this place and its inhabitants, says the Lord. I will make this city like Topheth.

The houses of Jerusalem and the houses of the kings of Judah will be defiled like the place of Topheth—all the houses on whose roofs they burned incense to all the heavenly hosts and poured out drink offerings to other gods.’”
Jeremiah returned from Topheth, where the LORD had sent him to prophesy. He stood in the courtyard of the LORD’s house and said to all the people:

“This is what the LORD Almighty, the God of Israel, says: Look, I am bringing on this city and all its towns every disaster I have pronounced against it, because they have stubbornly refused to listen to my words.”
Pashhur son of Immer, the priest who was the officer in charge of the LORD’s house, heard Jeremiah the prophet prophesying these words.
Pashhur struck Jeremiah the prophet and put him in the cell at the Upper Benjamin Gate in the LORD’s house.
The next day, Pashhur brought Jeremiah out of the cell. Jeremiah said to him, “The LORD has named you not Pashhur, but ‘An Exile and a Wanderer.’

For this is what the LORD says: Look, I am making you an exile—you and all your friends. They will fall by the sword of their enemies, and your own eyes will see it. I will hand all Judah over to the king of Babylon, and he will take them captive to Babylon and kill them with the sword.

I will hand over all the wealth of this city, all the fruit of its labor, all its precious possessions, and all the treasures of the kings of Judah. I will hand them over to their enemies, who will seize them, plunder them, and carry them to Babylon.
And you, Pashhur, and everyone living in your house will go into captivity. You will go to Babylon, and there you will die and be buried—you and all your friends to whom you prophesied falsely.”
You persuaded me, Lord, and I was persuaded. You overpowered me and prevailed over me. I have become a laughingstock all day long, and everyone mocks me.
Whenever I spoke and cried out, I called out against robbers and plunderers, for the word of the LORD brought me reproach and ridicule every day.
I said, “I will not remember him or speak in his name anymore.” But it became like a burning fire in my heart, hidden in my bones. I tried to bear it, but I could not.

For I heard the murmuring of many who gather around me. All who greet me with their mouths but hate me in their hearts say, “Expose him to us, and we will rise against him. Perhaps we can entice him and take our revenge on him.”

But the Lord is with me like a mighty warrior. Therefore all my persecutors will be ashamed and will not succeed. They are utterly ashamed because they did not act wisely, with an everlasting shame that will not be forgotten.
The mighty Lord examines righteousness and sees the innermost thoughts and the heart. Let me see your vengeance on them, for I have laid my case before you.
Praise the Lord! Praise the Lord, for he has rescued the life of the poor from the hands of evildoers.
Cursed is the day on which I was born! May the day my mother gave birth to me not be blessed!
Cursed is the man who brought my father the news, saying, “A son, a male child, has been born to you,” thinking he had made him very happy.
May that man be like the towns that the Lord overthrew without relenting. May he hear wailing in the morning and a battle cry at noon.
because he did not kill me in the womb, so that my mother would have been my grave and would have carried me in her womb forever.
Why did I come out of the womb to see toil and sorrow, and to have my days end in shame?
The word that came to Jeremiah from the Lord when King Zedekiah sent Pashhur son of Malchiah and Zephaniah son of Maaseiah, the priests, to him, saying:
“Inquire of the Lord for us, because Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon is fighting against us. Perhaps the Lord will act for us according to all his wonders and drive him away from us.”
Jeremiah said to them, “This is what you must say to King Zedekiah:

This is what the Lord, the God of Israel, says: “Look, I am turning back the weapons in your hands with which you are fighting the king of Babylon and the Chaldeans who are besieging you outside the city, and I will gather them inside this city.
“‘I myself will fight against you with a mighty hand and an uplifted arm, in anger, fury, and great wrath.
I will strike the inhabitants of this city, both people and animals. They will die in a great plague.

Afterward, says the Lord, I will hand over Zedekiah king of Judah, his servants, and the people who remain in this city after the sword, famine, and plague. I will hand them over to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, to their enemies, and to those who seek their lives. He will strike them down with the sword and will not spare them, show them pity, or have mercy on them.
And say to this people, “This is what the Lord says: Look, I am setting before you the way of life and the way of death.
Whoever stays in this city will die by the sword, famine, and plague. But whoever goes out to the Chaldeans who are besieging you will live and save his life.
For I have set my face against this city for harm and not for good, says the Lord. It will be handed over to the king of Babylon, and he will burn it with fire.”
And to the royal house of Judah: Hear the word of the Lord.

House of David, this is what the Lord says: “Administer justice in the morning, and rescue the oppressed from their oppressors. Otherwise my anger will break out like fire and burn with no one to extinguish it, because of your evil deeds.
Look, I am against you, you who dwell in the valley, in the deep plain, says the Lord, you who say, ‘Who will come against us? Who will enter our dwelling?’
I will punish you according to the fruit of your deeds, says the Lord. I will set fire to her towns, and it will consume everything around her.”
This is what the Lord says: ‘Go down to the palace of the king of Judah and speak this word there.
And say, “Hear the word of the Lord, king of Judah who sits on David’s throne—you, your servants, and your people who enter these gates.

This is what the Lord says: Administer justice and do what is right. Rescue the oppressed from their oppressors. Do not mistreat or oppress foreign residents, orphans, or widows, and do not shed innocent blood in this place.
If you truly carry out this command, kings who sit on David’s throne will enter the gates of this house, riding in chariots and on horses, each with his servants and his people.
But if you do not obey this command, I have sworn by myself, says the Lord, that this house will become a ruin.
For this is what the Lord says concerning the palace of the king of Judah: You are Gilead, the summit of Lebanon, but I will make you a wilderness, like uninhabited towns.
I will prepare destroyers against you, each with his axe in his hand. They will cut down your finest cedars and throw them into the fire.
Many nations will pass by this great city and say to one another, ‘Why has the Lord done this to this great city?’
And they will say, “Because they abandoned the covenant of the Lord their God, bowed down to other gods, and served them.”
Do not weep for the dead or mourn for him. Weep bitterly for the one who goes away and will never return or see the land where he was born.
For this is what the Lord says concerning Shallum son of Josiah, who became king in place of his father Josiah and went away from this place: He will never return there again.
Instead, he will die in the place where he was taken captive, and he will never see this land again.
Woe to the one who builds his house without righteousness and his upper rooms without justice, who makes his neighbor work for nothing and does not pay him his wages!
He says, “I will build myself a large house with spacious upper rooms.” He makes windows in them, roofs them with cedar, and paints pictures in them.
Are you a king because you delight in cedar? Your father ate and drank and administered justice and righteousness. Therefore I treated him well.
He upheld the cause of the poor and afflicted and did what was good. Whoever does these things knows me, says the Lord.
But your eyes and your heart are set on nothing except your own gain, on shedding innocent blood, and on committing oppression and injustice.

For this is what the LORD says about Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah: They will not mourn for him or say, “Alas, my brother! Alas, my brother!” They will not mourn for him, saying, “Alas, master! Alas, master!”
He will be buried as a donkey is buried: they will drag him away and throw him beyond the gates of Jerusalem.
Go up to Lebanon and cry out! Raise your voice in Bashan, and cry out from beyond the sea, for all your lovers have been crushed.
I spoke to you in your prosperity, but you said, “I will not listen.” This has been your way since your youth: you have not listened to my voice.
The wind will shepherd all your shepherds, and your lovers will go into captivity. Then you will be ashamed and humiliated because of all your wickedness.
You who live in Lebanon, who nest among the cedars, how you will groan when pains come upon you, and trembling like that of a woman giving birth!
As I live, says the LORD God, even if Jeconiah son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, were a signet ring on my right hand, I would tear you off from there.
I will hand you over to the people who seek your life and to those you fear—to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and to the Chaldeans.
I will throw you and the mother who bore you into another land, where neither of you was born, and there you will die.
You will not return to the land to which you long to return.
This man Jeconiah is despised and rejected, like a vessel that is of no use. For this reason he and his offspring have been taken away and thrown into a land they do not know.
Land, land, land, hear the word of the Lord!
