I will grant you mercy, have compassion on you, and settle you in your own land.
But if you say, “We will not stay in this land,” refusing to obey the voice of the LORD your God,
But if you say, “No! We will go into the land of Egypt, where we will not see war or hear the sound of the trumpet or go hungry for bread, and we will live there,”
then hear the word of the Lord, you remnant of Judah. This is what the Lord Almighty, the God of Israel, says: If you set your minds on entering Egypt and go there to live,
the sword you fear will overtake you there in the land of Egypt, and the famine you fear will pursue you there into Egypt, and there you will die.
All the men who set their minds on entering Egypt to live there will die by sword, famine, and plague. They will have no survivor who escapes the disaster I am bringing upon them.

For this is what the Lord Almighty, the God of Israel, says: Just as my anger and fury settled upon the inhabitants of Jerusalem, so my fury will settle upon you when you enter Egypt. You will become an object of cursing, horror, condemnation, and disgrace, and you will never see this place again.
The LORD has spoken concerning you, remnant of Judah: ‘Do not go into Egypt.’ Know that I have warned you today.
For you deceived yourselves when you sent me to the Lord your God and said, “Pray for us before the Lord our God, and tell us everything the Lord our God says to you, and we will do it.”
I have told you today, but you have not obeyed the voice of the Lord your God, and you have not done anything he sent me to tell you.
Now know that you will die by sword, famine, and plague in the place where you wanted to go and live.”
When Jeremiah finished telling all the people all the words of the Lord their God, which the Lord their God had sent him to them to speak—all these words—
Jezaniah son of Hoshaiah, Johanan son of Kareah, and all the wicked men said to Jeremiah, “You are lying! The Lord our God did not send you to tell us, ‘Do not enter Egypt to live there.’
Rather, Baruch son of Neriah is stirring you up against us, to hand us over to the Chaldeans so that they will kill us or take us captive to Babylon.”
Johanan son of Kareah, all the army commanders, and all the people did not obey the voice of the Lord by remaining in the land of Judah.
Johanan son of Kareah took all the army commanders and all the remnant who were left of the house of Judah,

The men, the women, the children, and the royal household—all the people whom Nebuzaradan, the captain of the guard, had left with Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan—as well as Jeremiah the prophet and Baruch son of Neriah.
They went to the land of Egypt because they had not obeyed the voice of the Lord, and they came as far as Tahpanhes.
The word of the Lord came to Jeremiah in Tahpanhes, saying:
Take large stones in your hand and bury them in the mortar of the brickwork at the entrance to Pharaoh’s palace in Tahpanhes, in the sight of the men of Judah.

Tell them: This is what the Lord Almighty, the God of Israel, says: Look, I am sending for Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, my servant, and bringing him here. He will set his throne above these stones that you have buried and raise his weapons over them.
He will come and strike the land of Egypt, consigning those destined for death to death, those destined for captivity to captivity, and those destined for the sword to the sword.

He will set fire to the temples of the gods of Egypt, burn them, and carry them away captive. He will wrap the land around himself as a shepherd wraps himself in his cloak, and he will leave there in peace.
He will break the pillar of Beth-shemesh in the land of Egypt, and he will burn the temples of the Egyptian gods with fire.
The word that came to Jeremiah from the Lord, to prophesy concerning all the Jews living in the land of Egypt, those living in Migdol, Tahpanhes, Memphis, and the land of Pathros.
This is what the Lord Almighty, the God of Israel, says: You have seen all the disaster I brought upon Jerusalem and all the towns of Judah. Today they lie in ruins, with no one living in them,
because of all the evil they did. They provoked me to anger by going and burning incense to other gods, whom neither they nor their ancestors had known.
I sent all my servants the prophets to them, taking care to send them, saying, “Do not do this detestable thing that I hate.”
But they did not listen or incline their ears to turn from their evil deeds and stop burning incense to other gods.
My anger and fury settled upon them, and fire blazed in the towns of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem. They became a ruin and an object of horror, as they are today.

And now this is what the Lord Almighty, the God of Israel, says: Why are you doing such great evil against yourselves, cutting off from among you the men, women, young people, and infants of Judah, leaving yourselves no descendants?

For you have provoked me to anger with the work of your hands and burned incense to other gods in the land of Egypt, where you have gone to live, so that I will destroy you and you will become an object of cursing and disgrace among all the nations of the earth.
Have you forgotten the evil of your ancestors, the evil of the kings of Judah, and the evil of their wives, which they committed in the land of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem?
They have not purified themselves to this day. They have not feared me or served me, nor have they followed my law and my covenant, which I gave to them and their ancestors.
Therefore this is what the Lord Almighty, the God of Israel, says: Look, I am setting my face against you to bring disaster and to destroy everyone belonging to the house of Judah.

I will crush the remnant of Judah who have set their faces toward entering Egypt to live there. They will all perish in the land of Egypt and die by sword, famine, and plague. They will become an object of curses, horror, condemnation, and disgrace.
I will punish those who live in the land of Egypt, just as I punished Jerusalem, with sword, famine, and plague.

There will be no escape or survival for the remnant of Judah who enter the land of Egypt to live there and hope in their hearts to return to the land of Judah. They will not return there, except for a few.

Then all the men who knew that their wives were burning incense to other gods, all the women standing there in a large assembly, and all the people living in the land of Egypt and in Pathros answered Jeremiah and said to him:
As for the word you have spoken to us in the name of the Lord, we will not listen to you.

But we will carry out every word that has come from our mouths: we will burn incense to the heavenly deity and pour out drink offerings to it, just as we, our ancestors, our kings, and our officials did in the towns of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem. Then we had plenty of bread, things went well for us, and we experienced no disaster.
But look, ever since we stopped burning incense to the heavenly deity and pouring out drink offerings to her, we have lacked everything and have been dying by sword and famine.

All the women answered and said, “When we burned incense to the Queen of Heaven and poured out drink offerings to her, it was not without our husbands that we made cakes for her and poured out drink offerings to her.”
Jeremiah said to all the people—to the men, the women, and all the people who had spoken these words to him:

That fragrant incense which you burned in the towns of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem—you, your ancestors, your kings, your officials, and the people of the land—was what the Lord remembered and took to heart.

The Lord could no longer forgive you because of your evil deeds and the abominations you committed. So your land became an object of horror and a curse, a desolate place without inhabitants, as it is today.
Because you burned incense and sinned against the Lord, and did not obey the Lord’s voice or follow his law, his covenant, and his decrees, this disaster has overtaken you, as it has today.
Jeremiah said to all the people, both men and women, “Hear the word of the Lord, all you people of Judah in the land of Egypt.

This is what the Lord Almighty, the God of Israel, says: You and your wives have spoken with your mouths and are carrying it out with your hands. You said, ‘We will fulfill the vows we made to burn incense to the heavenly deity and pour out drink offerings to her.’ You have confirmed your oaths and fulfilled your vows.

Therefore hear the word of the Lord, all you people of Judah living in the land of Egypt: Look, I have sworn by my great name, says the Lord, that my name will no longer be on the lips of anyone belonging to the house of Judah anywhere in the land of Egypt. They will no longer say, ‘As the Lord God lives.’
For I am hastening disaster upon them, says the Lord. All the men of Judah in the land of Egypt will perish by sword, famine, and plague, until I have finished them off.

Those who escape the sword will return from the land of Egypt to the land of Judah, few in number. Then the whole remnant of Judah who went to live in the land of Egypt will know whose word will stand, mine or theirs.
This will be the sign to you, says the Lord, that I am punishing you in this place, so that you may know that my words against you will surely stand and bring disaster.

This is what the Lord says: Look, I am handing over Pharaoh the Lame, king of Egypt, to his enemies and to those who seek his life, just as I handed over Zedekiah king of Judah to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, his enemy who sought his life.
The word that Jeremiah spoke to Baruch son of Neriah when he wrote these words on a scroll at Jeremiah’s dictation, in the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah:
This is what the Lord Almighty, the God of Israel, says concerning you, Baruch:
You said, “Woe to me, for the Lord has added sorrow to my pain! I am worn out with my groaning and have found no rest.”
Say this to him: This is what the Lord says: Look, what I built I am tearing down, and what I planted I am uprooting. I am laying waste the whole land.

But you have sought great things for yourself. Do not seek things that are beyond you, for look, I am bringing disaster upon all humanity, says the Lord. But I will grant you escape with your life wherever you go.
The word of the Lord came to Jeremiah the prophet, that he should prophesy concerning the nations.

Concerning the Egyptians and the army of Pharaoh the Lame, king of Egypt, which was camped by the River Euphrates at Carchemish, and which Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon defeated in the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah:
This is what the LORD Almighty, the God of Israel, says: Take up weapons and shields, and advance to battle.
Muster the horses! Mount the horsemen! Put on helmets! Polish the spears! Put on armor!
For I have seen them shattered and turning back. Their warriors were struck down and fled without looking back, because they were surrounded on every side, says the LORD.
The swift will not flee, nor will the mightiest of warriors escape. Beside the Euphrates River they all stumbled and fell.
Who is this rising like the river, whose waters surge like rivers?
The king of Egypt rises like a river, and his waters surge like rivers. He said, “I will rise and cover the earth; I will destroy the city and its inhabitants.”
Mount the horses! Glory in the chariots! Let the warriors march out: the Cushites and the people of Put who carry shields, and the Lydians who know how to shoot the bow.

That day will belong to the mighty LORD, a day of vengeance when he takes vengeance on his enemies. The sword will devour and be satisfied and drink its fill of their blood, for the mighty LORD will bring destruction in the northern land beside the Euphrates River.
Go up to Gilead and get balm, virgin daughter of Egypt. In vain you have multiplied your remedies; no help has come to you.
The nations have heard of your disgrace, and your wailing has filled the earth, because one warrior crashed into another, and both fell by the sword.
The word that the LORD spoke to Jeremiah the prophet concerning the coming of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon to lay waste the land of Egypt.
Declare it in Egypt and proclaim it in Migdol; proclaim it in Memphis and Tahpanhes. Say, “Prepare yourselves and get ready, for the sword has devoured everything around you.”
Why were your mighty men swept away? They fell and did not stand, because the Lord overthrew them.
Many of them were overthrown; one man even fell over another. They said, “Get up! Let us return to our people and to the land where we were born, away from the devastating sword.”
There they called Pharaoh, the lame king of Egypt, “An uproar who lets the appointed times pass.”
As I live, says the LORD, the King whose name is Sabaoth, Pharaoh will surely fall like a mountain breaking apart and like Carmel into the sea.
Pack your belongings for captivity, virgin daughter of Egypt, for Memphis will become a ruin and lie desolate, with no one living there.
Egypt is a beautiful, adorned heifer. An army from the north has come against her.

Her hired soldiers within her are like fattened calves. They too turned and fled together without standing their ground, because the day of their disaster had come upon them, the time of their punishment.
The sound of the army is like a snake slithering, for they will march in force and come against her with axes, like woodcutters.
Cut down her thickets, says the LORD, for there is no end to them. They are more numerous than locusts and cannot be counted.
The daughter of Egypt has been put to shame and handed over to the people of the north.
The mighty LORD, the God of Israel, says: Look, I am bringing punishment on Amon of the waters, on Pharaoh, on Egypt, on her gods, on her army, on her kings, on Pharaoh, and on all who trust in him.
I will hand them over to their enemies and to those who seek their lives, to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and his servants. Afterward she will be inhabited as in former days, says the LORD.

But you, my servant Jacob, do not be afraid, says the LORD; do not be dismayed, Israel. Look, I will save you from far away, and your descendants from the land of their captivity. Jacob will return and be at peace, quiet, and at rest, with no one to frighten him.

But you, my servant Jacob, do not be afraid, says the LORD, because I am with you. I will make an end of all the nations among whom I scattered you, but I will not make an end of you. I will discipline you justly, and I will certainly not leave you unpunished.
The word of the LORD came to Jeremiah the prophet, telling him to prophesy against the Philistines before Pharaoh struck Gaza.

This is what the LORD says: Look, I am bringing young men from the north. They will be like an overflowing torrent and will sweep away the land and everything in it, the city and its inhabitants. People will groan, and all the inhabitants of the land will wail.

At the sound of the trampling hooves of his mighty horses, at the shaking of his chariots and the noise of his wheels, fathers did not turn back for their children, because their hands had become weak.
Look, the day is coming to plunder all the Philistines and to destroy Tyre and Sidon and all who remain to help. For the LORD is laying waste the Philistines, the remnant of the Cappadocian islands.
“A blow has fallen on Gaza. Ashkelon has been shattered, along with everyone left in their settlements.”
O sword of the LORD, how long will you remain restless and not rest from destroying? Withdraw into your sheath; withdraw and be still!
How can it be still when the Lord has commanded it against Ashkelon and the seacoasts? There he has given it authority.
Concerning Moab.
This is what the mighty LORD, the God of Israel, says: Woe to Nebo, for she has been plundered! Kiriathaim has been put to shame and disgraced. Her strength has been put to shame and scattered.
Moab has no more glory. In Heshbon they plotted evil against her and said, “Come, let us destroy her as a nation.” Even if you remain completely silent, the sword will pursue you.
A sound of wailing from Horonaim: plunder and great destruction!
Moab is shattered; its poor have raised a wail.
On the ascent to Luhith they will go up weeping, and on the descent to Horonaim they will make distress and cries of destruction heard.
Flee and save your lives! Be like a root in the wilderness.
Because you trusted in your strongholds and your treasures, you too will be captured. Chemosh will go into captivity, together with his priests and his officials.
The plunderer will come against all your towns, and they will not escape. The valley will perish, and the plain will be devastated, just as the Lord has said.
Give Moab a crown, because she will be utterly devastated, and all her towns will become ruins, with no one living in them.
Cursed is anyone who does the Lord’s work deceitfully, and cursed is anyone who keeps his sword from bloodshed.

The Moabites have been at ease since their youth, resting undisturbed on their sediment. They have not been poured from one vessel into another, nor have they gone into captivity. Therefore their flavor remains in them, and their scent has not faded.
Therefore, look, the days are coming, says the Lord, when I will send plunderers against them. They will plunder them, empty their vessels, and smash their jars.
Moab will be ashamed of Chemosh, just as the Israelites were ashamed of Bethel, in which they trusted.
How can you say, ‘We are warriors, mighty men in battle’?
Moab has been plundered, and her towns [?]. The chosen men among her warriors have been handed over to slaughter, says the King, whose name is the Lord, the mighty God.
Moab’s destruction is near, and its disaster is coming very quickly.
Be distressed and tremble, all you who surround him and all who know his name. Say, “How the mighty staff has been broken, the glorious rod!”
Come down from honor and sit in disgrace, you who live in daughter Dibon [?], because Moab’s plunderer has advanced against you and destroyed your fortifications.
Stand beside the roads and watch, you who inhabit Aroer [?]. Ask the one fleeing and the one escaping; say, ‘What has happened?’
Moab is ashamed because it has been shattered. Wail and cry out in Arnon, because Moab has been shattered.
Judgment has come upon the land of the plateau, upon Holon, Jahzah, and Mephaath,
upon Dibon [?], Nebo, and Beth-diblathaim,
upon Kiriathaim, Beth-gamul, and Beth-meon,
upon Kerioth, Bozrah, and all the towns of the land of Moab, far and near.
Moab’s horn has been cut off, and its arm has been broken, says the Lord.
Make him sick, because he has exalted himself against the Lord. Moab will wallow in his vomit, and he too will become a laughingstock.
Was not Israel a laughingstock to you? Was he found among thieves when you were waging war against him?
Leave the towns and settle among the cliffs, inhabitants of Moab. Be like a dove that nests on a rocky ledge.
We have heard of the leaders of Moab, who are very proud—their pride, their arrogance, and the haughtiness of their hearts.
“I know,” says the Lord, “their deeds, which were not righteous; and his diviners did not predict this about him.”
Therefore wail over Moab, and cry out from every place over all Moab. They will lament the disaster that has befallen the people living in his house.

I will weep for you more than the weeping for Jazer, vine of Sibmah. Your branches crossed the sea and reached as far as the sea of Jazer, because the plunderer has fallen upon your harvest and your grape gathering.

Joy and gladness will pass away from the land of Carmel and from the land of Moab. Wine will cease from the winepress. Those who tread the grapes will not tread them, nor will they sing or say, “Hey! Hey!”

From the wailing of Heshbon as far as Elealeh and Jahaz, they have raised their voices, from Zoar as far as Horonaim and as far as the fortified town of Elas, the three-year-old heifer, because the waters of Nimrim will dry up.
“I will put an end in Moab,” says the Lord, “to anyone who offers a burnt offering and burns incense to his god.”
Therefore my heart will sound like a harp over Moab, because they did evil and perished.
For their heads are shaved and their beards cut short. There are cuts on all their hands, and sackcloth around their waists.
On all the rooftops of Moab and throughout all its streets there is mourning, because I have broken Moab like a vessel that is of no use, says the Lord.
How they have been shattered and have wailed! How Moab has turned his back in shame! Moab will become an object of ridicule and dismay to everyone around him.
This is what the Lord says: Look, he will rise and soar like an eagle and spread his wings over Moab.
Kerioth has been captured, and the fortress has been conquered. On that day the hearts of Moab’s warriors will be like the heart of a woman suffering the pains of childbirth.
Moab will cease to be a people, because he exalted himself against the Lord.
Terror, a pit, and a trap await you, inhabitant of Moab, says the Lord.

Whoever flees from the sound of terror will fall into the pit, and whoever climbs out of the pit will be caught in the trap, because I am bringing these things upon Moab in the year of their punishment, says the Lord.
For fire has come out of Heshbon, and a flame from Sihon’s fortified town. It will consume the border of Moab and the leaders of the people of tumult.
Woe to you, Moab! You have perished, people of Chemosh, for your sons and daughters have been scattered into captivity.
“But I will restore Moab’s captives in the last days,” says the Lord. Here ends the judgment of Moab.
Concerning the Ammonites.
This is what the Lord says: “Does Israel have no sons? Does he have no heirs? Why has Milcom taken possession of Gad, and why do his people live in its towns?”

Therefore, look, the days are coming, says the Lord, when I will make the sound of battle heard against Rabbah of the Ammonites. It will become a ruined mound, and its villages will be burned with fire. Israel will take possession of those who took possession of him, says the Lord.

Wail, Heshbon, because Ai has been destroyed! Cry out, villages of Rabbah! Put on sackcloth, beat yourselves, and cut yourselves with blades, because Milcom will go into captivity, together with his priests and his officials, says the Lord.
Why do you boast about your valleys and trust in your ravines, beloved daughter, who trusts in her treasures and says, “Who will come against me?”
Look, I am bringing terror upon you from everyone around you, says the Lord Almighty. I will scatter them, each in a different direction, and no one will gather the scattered.
But afterward I will restore the captives of the Ammonites, says the Lord.
This is what the Lord Almighty says: There is no longer any wisdom in Teman. Counsel has vanished from the discerning; their wisdom has been taken away.
Flee, turn back, and dwell in deep places, inhabitants of Dedan, because I have brought Esau’s destruction upon him, the time of his punishment, says the Lord.
If grape gatherers came against you, would they not leave gleanings? And if thieves came at night, they would destroy as much as they wished.
For I have searched out Esau and exposed his hiding places. He hid himself and was not found. His descendants, his brothers, and his neighbors have been scattered, and they are no more.
Leave your orphans; I will keep them alive. Let your widows trust in me.

For this is what the Lord says: Look, those who were not required to drink the cup have drunk it. Did you think you would escape punishment? You will not escape punishment; you too will drink the cup.
For I have sworn by myself, says the Lord, that Bozrah will become an object of horror, a ruin, a disgrace, and a curse. All her towns will be ruins forever.
I have heard news from the Lord, and a messenger has been sent to the nations: Rise up! Let us go up against her for battle!
For look, I have made you small among the nations and despised among humankind.

Your wickedness and the pride of your heart have deceived you, you who live in the cleft of the rock and hold the heights of the hill, saying in your heart, ‘Who will bring me down to the ground?’ Even if you place your nest among the stars, even if you raise your nest high like an eagle, I will bring you down from there, says the Lord.
Edom will become a ruin. Everyone who passes by her will be appalled and hiss at all her wounds.
You will be overthrown as God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah, says the Lord. No one will live there, and no human being will dwell there.

Look, he will come up like a lion from the thickets of the Jordan against the secure pasture. I will quickly drive them away from it and appoint troops over it. For who is like me? Who can testify against me? What shepherd can stand before me?

Therefore hear the Lord’s plan, which he has devised against Edom, and his purposes, which he has devised against the inhabitants of Teman: the smallest of the flock will drag them away and lay their pasture waste because of them.
At the sound of their downfall the earth trembled. Her wailing—its sound was heard from the Red Sea.
Look, he will rise and soar like an eagle and spread his wings over Bozrah. On that day the hearts of Edom’s warriors will be like the heart of a woman suffering the pains of childbirth.
Hamath and Arpad are ashamed, because they have heard bad news and are crushed. Her terror is in the sea, and she has found no rest.
Damascus has grown weak and turned to flee. Trembling has seized her; distress and pains have gripped her like a woman giving birth.
How has the celebrated city, the joyful city, not been abandoned?
Therefore her troops will fall in her streets, and all her fighting men will be silenced on that day, says the Lord Almighty.
I will release fire in the streets of Damascus, and it will consume the fortresses of Ben-hadad.
This is what the Lord says: Rise up, advance against Kedar, and plunder the people of the east.
They will take their tents and their flocks. They will carry off their tent curtains, all their belongings, and their camels. They will summon attackers against them from all around them.

Flee, wander far away, and dwell in deep places, inhabitants of Hazor, says the Lord. For Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon has devised a plan against them and formed a purpose against them, and has said:
Rise, advance against a prosperous people who live undisturbed, says the Lord, who have neither gates nor bars and live alone.

Their camels will become plunder, and their abundant livestock will become spoil. I will scatter them—the people who clip their hair at the temples—to every wind. I will bring their destruction from every side, says the Lord.
Hazor will become a dwelling place for jackals, a ruin forever. No one will live there, and no human being will dwell there.
The word of the Lord that came to Jeremiah the prophet, to prophesy against Elam, at the beginning of the reign of Zedekiah king of Judah.
This is what the Lord Almighty says: Look, I am breaking the bow of Elam, the chief source of their strength.
I will bring four winds against Elam from the four corners of heaven, and I will scatter them to all these winds. There will be no nation where the scattered people of Elam are not found.

I will shatter Elam before their enemies and before those who seek their lives. I will bring disaster upon them, my fierce anger, says the Lord. I will send the sword among them until I have destroyed them completely.
I will set my throne in Elam and destroy kings and rulers from there, says the Lord.
But in the last days I will bring back the captives of Elam, says the Lord.
The word that the Lord spoke against Babylon and against the land of the Chaldeans through Jeremiah the prophet.

Declare it among the nations and proclaim it. Raise a banner; proclaim it and do not conceal it. Say: Babylon has been captured! Bel has fallen, and Merodach has been disgraced. Her idols are ashamed, and her carved images have been shattered.
For a nation has come up against her from the north. It will turn her land into a wasteland, and no one will live in it. Humans and animals alike have fled and gone away.
In those days and at that time, says the Lord, the people of Israel and the people of Judah will come together, walking and weeping and seeking the Lord their God.
They will ask about the roads to Zion, with their faces turned toward her: “Come, let us join ourselves to the Lord in an everlasting covenant that will not be forgotten.”
My people have been like lost sheep. Their shepherds led them astray and scattered them on the mountains. They went from mountain to hill and forgot their resting place.

Everyone who found them devoured them, and their enemies say, “We will not spare them, because they sinned against the Lord and against his righteous dwelling place. The Lord is the hope of their ancestors.”
Flee from within Babylon! Leave the land of the Chaldeans, and be like male goats leading the flock.

For look, I am stirring up and bringing against Babylon assemblies of many nations from the northern land. They will line up against her, and from there she will be captured. Their arrows are like a successful warrior who does not return empty-handed.
The land of the Chaldeans will become plunder, and all who plunder her will have their fill, says the Lord.
Because you rejoice and because you exult, O head of my inheritance, and you leap like fattened calves and dance like rams of the flock.
Your mother is deeply ashamed, and the one who gave birth to you is disgraced. Look, she is the last of the nations, like a wilderness, ruined and desolate.
Because of the Lord’s anger, she will not be inhabited but will be entirely desolate. Everyone who passes by Babylon will be astonished and hiss at all her wounds.
Line up against Babylon, all you who know how to shoot a bow. Shoot at her; do not spare your arrows, because she has sinned against the Lord.

Raise a battle cry against her from all around her! She has surrendered. Her foundations have fallen; her walls have been torn down. For this is the Lord’s retribution. Take vengeance on her; do to her as she has done.

Destroy the sower from Babylon, and the one who holds the sickle at harvesttime. Because of the sword that brings suffering, everyone will turn back to their own people, and everyone will flee to their own land.
Israel is a wandering sheep; lions have driven them astray. First the king of Assyria devoured him, and this last one, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, proved stronger than he.
Therefore this is what the Lord Almighty, the God of Israel, says: Look, I am punishing the king of Babylon and his land, just as I punished the king of Assyria.
I will bring Israel back to their pasture. They will graze in Carmel and Bashan, on the mountain of Ephraim and in Gilead, and they will be satisfied.

In those days and at that time, says the Lord Almighty, Israel’s guilt will be sought, but it will not exist, and Judah’s sin will not be found, because I will forgive the remnant who remain among them.
Go up against the rebellious land! Go up against her and against her inhabitants! Awake, O sword, and destroy them, says the Lord, and do as I commanded you.
The sound of someone calling in the land, and great destruction!
How the mighty power of the whole earth has been broken and swept away! How Babylon has become an object of astonishment among the nations!
You have been tripped up, Babylon, and you have also been captured. You did not know that you had risen against the Lord.
The Lord has opened his treasury and brought out the weapons of his anger, because the Lord God Almighty has work to do in the land of the Chaldeans.
Come against her from every side. Open her gates; strip her like a naked woman and destroy her. Leave her no remnant.
Destroy her, and let all her fruits be handed over to slaughter. Woe to them, because their day has arrived, the time of their punishment!
The sound of those fleeing and escaping from the land of Babylon, to announce in Zion the vengeance of the Lord our God, vengeance for his temple!

Summon many against Babylon, all who know how to shoot a bow. Shoot at her from every side, and leave her no remnant. Repay her as she deserves; do to her everything she has done, because she has acted arrogantly against the Lord, against the Holy One of Israel.
Therefore her troops will fall within her, and all her fighting men will be silenced on that day.
Look, I am against you, arrogant one, says the Lord God Almighty, for your day has arrived, the time of your punishment.
The arrogant one will be overthrown and fall, with no one to raise him up. I will set fire to her towns, and it will consume everything around him.
This is what the Lord of hosts says: The people of Israel and the people of Judah are oppressed together. All who took them captive hold them fast and refuse to let them go.
Their redeemer is strong; the Lord Almighty is his name. He will surely plead their case, give rest to the earth, and trouble all the inhabitants of the world.
A sword against the Chaldeans, says the Lord, and against all the inhabitants of Babylon, against her officials and against her wise men!
A sword against her diviners, and they will become confused! A sword against her warriors, and they will be shattered!
A sword against her horses and her chariots, and against all the foreigners living within her! They will become like women. A sword against her treasures, and they will be plundered!
A sword against her waters, and they will dry up! For it is a land of carved images, and they boast in idols.
Therefore sirens will dwell in her, and ostriches will live in her. She will never again be inhabited or settled, from generation to generation.
It will be like Sodom and Gomorrah, which God overthrew along with their inhabitants. No one will settle there, and no human being will live there.
Look, a people is coming from the north, a great people, and many kings will be stirred up from the ends of the earth.
They are armed with bows and spears. They are cruel and have no mercy. Their voices roar like the raging sea. They ride horses, prepared like warriors for battle against you, daughter Babylon.
The king of Babylon has heard the report about them, and his hands have gone limp. Distress has seized him, and pains like those of a woman giving birth.

Look, he will come up like a lion from the thickets of the Jordan against a secure pasture. For I will quickly drive them out of it, and I will appoint troops over it. For who is like me? Who can challenge me? What shepherd can stand against me?

Therefore, hear the plan the Lord has devised against Babylon and the purpose he has formed against the land of the Chaldeans: the smallest of the flock will drag them away, and their pasture will be devastated because of them.
At the news that Babylon had been captured, the earth shook; her wailing was heard among the nations.
This is what the Lord God Almighty says: Look, I am stirring up a hard heart and a destroying spirit against Babylon and its inhabitants.
I will send plunderers against Babylon, and they will plunder it and trample its land. They will gather against it from every side on the day of disaster.
Let the archer not stop shooting, and let the warrior not take off his armor. Do not spare its troops; destroy its entire army.
The slain will fall in the land of the Chaldeans, and the wounded in her streets.
For Israel and Judah have not been left widowed by their God, by the Lord Almighty, their God, though their land was filled with injustice before the Holy One of Israel.

Flee from Babylon, and let each person save his own life. Do not be swept away because of its sins, for this is the time of the Lord's retribution against it. He is repaying it according to its deeds.
Babylon was a golden cup in the Lord's hand, making the whole earth drunk. All the nations drank its wine and went mad.
Suddenly Babylon has fallen and been plundered. Wail over her! Bring medicines for her wounds; perhaps she will be healed.
We tried to heal Babylon, but it was not healed. Let us leave it and go, each to his own land, for its judgment has reached heaven and risen to the clouds.
The Lord has brought about our vindication. Come, let us recount in Zion the deeds of the Lord our God.
Gather the shields; stock up on arrows. The Lord has stirred up the spirit of the king of Media, for his plan is to destroy Babylon. This is the Lord's retribution, vengeance for his temple.
Raise a banner against Babylon's walls. Set a watch and drown it in water, for the Lord has carried out what he planned against Babylon.
You who lived beside abundant waters, your treasures are many. Your end has come, and your wound has grown severe.
The Lord Almighty has sworn by himself: I will fill you with people like locusts, and they will raise a shout over you, saying, 'Ah! Ah!'
The Lord made the earth by his power, established the world by his wisdom, and stretched out the heavens by his understanding.
He makes the waters roar in the heavens. He brings clouds up from the ends of the earth. He makes lightning for the rain and brings the winds out of his storehouses.
Everyone is foolish, without knowledge. All metalworkers are put to shame by the carved images they have made, for what they have cast is a lie, and there is no breath in them.
They are nothing, works of foolishness. When the time comes for them to be punished, they will perish.
Jacob's portion is not like these. Rather, the one who created everything is their portion and the scepter of their inheritance. The Lord Almighty is his name.
Prepare weapons of war for me! With you I will scatter nations, and with you I will destroy kingdoms.
With you I will scatter horses and their riders, and with you I will scatter chariots and those who ride in them.
With you I will scatter men and women. With you I will scatter the old and the young. With you I will scatter soldiers and young women.
With you I will scatter the shepherd and his flock, with you I will scatter the farmer and his team of oxen, and with you I will scatter rulers and governors.
I will repay Babylon and all the inhabitants of Chaldea for all the evil they committed in Zion before your eyes, says the Lord.
Look, I am against you, destroying mountain, says the Lord, you who destroy the whole earth. I will stretch out my hand against you, roll you down from the rock, and make you a burned mountain.
They will not take from you a stone for a corner or a stone for a foundation. Instead, you will be a ruin forever, says the Lord.

Raise a banner in the land. Sound the trumpet among the nations. Prepare the nations against it. Summon against it the kingdoms of Ararat, Armenia, and Ashkenaz. Appoint a destroyer against it. Bring up horses like locusts.
Prepare nations against her—the king of Media, his nobles, and all his governors.
The earth will quake and tremble, for the Lord's purpose against Babylon stands: to devastate the land of Babylon so that no one lives there.

The warriors of Babylon have stopped fighting against those living in the fortresses. Their strength has been broken, and they have become like women. Its dwellings have been uprooted, and its gates have been broken.
Runner will run to meet runner, and messenger to meet messenger, to tell the king of Babylon that his city has been captured on every side.
Its crossings have been seized, its marshes have been burned with fire, and all its warriors are terrified.
For this is what the Lord Almighty, the God of Israel, says: Daughter Babylon is like a threshing floor whose time for threshing has arrived. In a little while, its harvest will come.

Jerusalem said, “Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon has devoured me and plundered me. He has left me like an empty vessel. He has swallowed me like a dragon, filled his belly with my delicacies, and led me astray.”
“My plunder and my possessions were carried off to Babylon, and my blood is on the inhabitants of Chaldea,” Jerusalem will say.
Therefore this is what the Lord says: “Look, I will plead your case and take vengeance for you. I will dry up Babylon’s sea and make its springs dry.”
Babylon will become a ruin, a dwelling for jackals, an object of horror and hissing, with no one living in it.
They will roar like lions and growl like lion cubs.
“In anger I will prepare their drinking feast and make them drunk. They will be shattered and sleep forever, never to wake,” says the Lord.
“I will hand them over like fattened animals for killing, like rams and young goats for slaughter.
How [?], the praise of the whole earth, has been captured! How Babylon has become an object of horror among the nations!
The sea has risen over Babylon, and it has been covered by its many waves.
Her towns have become an object of horror, like a ruined and desolate land. No one will live in them, and no human being will dwell in them.
“I will punish Bel in Babylon and bring his plunder out of his mouth. The nations will no longer fear him, and Babylon’s broad walls will also fall.
Come out of it, my people! Each of you, save your life from the fierce anger of the Lord.

“Do not let your hearts fail or be afraid because of the report heard in the land. A report will come in one year, and after that year another report. There will be violence in the land, and ruler will rise against ruler.”
“Therefore, look, the days are coming,” says the Lord, “when I will punish Babylon’s carved idols. The whole land will perish, and all her slain will fall within her.”
Heaven and earth and everything in them will rejoice over Babylon, because plunderers will come against her from the north, says the Lord.
“In Babylon too the slain of Israel will fall, and because of Babylon the slain will fall throughout the earth.
You who have escaped the sword, go on; do not stop. Remember the Lord from far away, and let Jerusalem come to mind. And the house of Israel will say:
“We are deeply ashamed because we have heard insults, and shame has covered our faces, because foreigners have entered the Lord’s sanctuary.”
“Therefore, look, the days are coming,” says the Lord, “when I will punish Babylon and her carved idols, and throughout her land her slain will fall.
“Even if Babylon rises to heaven and sets her stronghold on high, plunderers will come against her from me,” says the Lord.
The sound of wailing comes from Babylon, and great destruction from the land of the Chaldeans.
For the Lord has plundered Babylon and destroyed both people and livestock within her—a great roar, like mighty waters whose sound carries far.
For plunderers have come against Babylon. Her warriors have been captured, and their bows have been broken, because the Lord is a God who repays; he will certainly repay them.
“I will make her princes, her wise men, her nobles, her rulers, and her warriors drunk. They will sleep forever and never wake,” says the King, whose name is the Lord Almighty.

This is what the Lord Almighty says: “Babylon’s broad walls will be completely uprooted, and her high gates will be burned with fire. Peoples will labor for nothing, and nations will be ravaged by fire.”

The instruction that Jeremiah the prophet gave to Seraiah son of Neriah, son of Mahseiah, when he went with Zedekiah king of Judah to Babylon in the eleventh year of his reign. Seraiah was in charge of the camp.
Jeremiah wrote in a single scroll all the disaster that was coming upon Babylon—all these words written against Babylon.
Jeremiah said to Seraiah, “When you enter Babylon, read and examine all these words.”
And he said, “Lord, you have spoken against this place, to destroy it so that no one will live in it, neither people nor livestock, for it will be a ruin forever.”
When you have finished reading this scroll, tie a stone to it and throw it into the Euphrates.
Here end the words of Jeremiah.
Zedekiah was twenty-one years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem for eleven years. His mother’s name was Hamutal, daughter of Jeremiah, from Libnah.
He did what was evil in the LORD’s sight, just as Jehoiakim had done.
Because of these things, the Lord’s anger came upon Jerusalem and Judah until he cast them out of his presence. And King Zedekiah rebelled against Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon.

In the ninth year of his reign, in the tenth month, in that very month, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came against Jerusalem, he and his entire army. They camped against it and built siegeworks all around it.
The city remained under siege until the eleventh year of King Zedekiah.
In the seventh month, on the ninth day of the month, the famine became severe in the city, and there was no bread for the people of the land.

The city wall was breached, and all the fighting men fled. They left the city at night by way of the gate between the walls beside the king’s garden, while the Chaldeans surrounded the city. They went by the road to the plain.
The Chaldean army pursued the king and overtook Zedekiah in the plain of Jericho. His entire army scattered and deserted him.
They captured the king and brought him up to the king of Babylon at Riblah, in the land of Hamath, and he pronounced judgment on him.
The king of Babylon slaughtered Zedekiah’s sons before his eyes, and he put all the nobles of Judah to the sword at Riblah.
The king of Babylon put out Zedekiah’s eyes, bound him in chains, and took him to Babylon. He confined him in prison until the day he died.

In the fifth month, on the tenth day of the month, in the nineteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, Nebuzaradan, the chief executioner, came and stood before the king of Babylon in Jerusalem.
He burned the house of the Lord, the palace of the king of Judah, and all the houses of Jerusalem. They burned all the houses of the leading men with fire.
The entire Chaldean army that was with the commander of the guard demolished all the walls around Jerusalem.
Nebuzaradan took captive some of the poor people, the rest of the people who remained in the city, those who had deserted to the king of Babylon, and the rest of the people.
But Nebuzaradan, the commander of the guard, left some of the poor people of the land to tend the vineyards and work the land.
The Chaldeans broke up the bronze pillars, the basins, and the bronze Sea in the house of the Lord. They took all their bronze and carried it to Babylon.
They also took the pots, the shovels, the axes, the basins, the spoons, and all the bronze utensils used in the service.
The chief executioner also took the [?], the censers, the forks, the pots, the bowls, the lampstands, the spoons, and the dishes made of gold and silver.
There were two bronze pillars, one Sea, and twelve bronze bulls beneath the sides of the Sea, which King Solomon had made for the house of the Lord. The bronze of these objects was beyond weighing.
As for those two pillars, one pillar was eighteen cubits high, and a cord twelve cubits long went all the way around it. It was four fingerbreadths thick and hollow inside.

A bronze capital stood on top of it, and the height of one capital was five cubits. There was latticework and pomegranates all around the capital, all made of bronze. The other pillar and its pomegranates were like these.
There were ninety-six pomegranates; there were one hundred pomegranates in all on the latticework all around.
The captain of the guard took Seraiah the chief priest, Zephaniah the second priest, and the three gatekeepers.

From the city he took one eunuch who was in command of the fighting men, seven prominent men who appeared before the king and had remained in the city, the scribe and the commander of the army of the people of the land, and sixty men from the people of the land who were found inside the city.
Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard took them and brought them to the king of Babylon at Riblah in the land of Hamath.
The king of Babylon struck them down and killed them at Riblah in the land of Hamath. So Judah was taken captive from its land.
These are the people whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon took captive: in the seventh year of his reign, 3,023 Jews.
In the eighteenth year of the reign of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, he took 832 people captive from Jerusalem.
In the twenty-third year of Nebuchadnezzar, Nebuzaradan, the chief executioner, took 745 Jewish people captive. There were 4,600 people in all.

In the thirty-seventh year of the captivity of Jehoiachin king of Judah, in the twelfth month, on the twenty-fifth day of the month, Evil-merodach king of Babylon, in the year he became king, restored Jehoiachin king of Judah to favor and brought him out of prison.
He spoke kindly to him and placed his throne above the thrones of the kings who were with him in Babylon.
Jehoiachin changed out of his prison clothes and ate regularly in the king’s presence all the days of his life.
His allowance was issued regularly each day by the king of Babylon until the day he died, throughout all the days of his life.
